45_8_28: And we know that God causes all things to work together for good to those who love God — to those who are called according to His purpose.
45_8_29: For those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to become conformed to the image of His Son — so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
45_8_30: And these whom He predestined, He also called. And these whom He called, He also justified. And these whom He justified, He also glorified.
45_8_31: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
45_8_32: He who did not spare His own Son, but delivered Him over for us all — how will He not also with Him freely give us all things?
45_8_33: Who will bring a charge against God's elect? God is the One who justifies.
45_8_34: Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is He who died — yes, rather who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.
45_8_35: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
45_8_36: Just as it is written: "For Your sake we are being put to death all day long; we were considered as sheep to be slaughtered."
45_8_37: But in all these things we overwhelmingly conquer through Him who loved us.
45_8_38: For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
45_8_39: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
45_9_1: I am telling the truth in Christ; I am not lying — my conscience testifies with me in the Holy Spirit —
45_9_2: that I have great sorrow and unceasing grief in my heart.
45_9_3: For I could wish that I myself were accursed, separated from Christ, for the sake of my brothers — my kinsmen according to the flesh.
45_9_4: Who are Israelites — to whom belongs the adoption as sons, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the Law, and the temple service, and the promises;
45_9_5: whose are the fathers — and from whom is the Christ according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.
45_9_6: But it is not as though the word of God has failed. For they are not all Israel who are descended from Israel.
45_9_7: Nor are they all children, because they are Abraham's descendants — but, "Through Isaac your descendants will be named."
45_9_8: That is — it is not the children of the flesh who are children of God. But the children of the promise are regarded as descendants.
45_9_9: For this is the word of promise: "At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son."
45_9_10: And not only this — but there was Rebekah also, when she had conceived twins by one man, our father Isaac.
45_9_11: For though the twins were not yet born, and had not done anything good or bad — so that God's purpose according to His choice would stand, not because of works, but because of Him who calls —
45_9_12: it was said to her: "The older will serve the younger."
45_9_13: Just as it is written: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."
45_9_14: What shall we say then? There is no injustice with God, is there? May it never be!
45_9_15: For He says to Moses: "I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion."
45_9_16: So then it does not depend on the man who wills, or the man who runs — but on God who has mercy.
45_9_17: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: "For this very purpose I raised you up — to demonstrate My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed throughout the whole earth."
45_9_18: So then He has mercy on whom He desires — and He hardens whom He desires.
45_9_19: You will say to me then, "Why does He still find fault? For who resists His will?"
45_9_20: On the contrary, who are you, O man, who answers back to God? The thing molded will not say to the molder, "Why did you make me like this," will it?
45_9_21: Or does not the potter have a right over the clay — to make from the same lump one vessel for honorable use, and another for common use?
45_9_22: What if God — although willing to demonstrate His wrath, and to make His power known — endured with much patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction?
45_9_23: And He did so to make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory.
45_9_24: Even us — whom He also called, not from among Jews only, but also from among Gentiles.
45_9_25: As He says also in Hosea: "I will call those who were not My people, 'My people' — and her who was not beloved, 'Beloved.'"
45_9_26: "And it shall be that in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not My people' — there they shall be called sons of the living God."
45_9_27: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
45_9_28: For the Lord will execute His word on the earth, completely and quickly."
45_9_29: And just as Isaiah foretold: "Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left to us a posterity, we would have become like Sodom — and would have resembled Gomorrah."
45_9_30: What shall we say then? That Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, attained righteousness — even the righteousness which is by faith.
45_9_31: But Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not arrive at that law.
45_9_32: Why? Because they did not pursue it by faith, but as though it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone —
45_9_33: just as it is written: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offense — and he who believes in Him will not be put to shame."
45_10_1: Brothers, my heart's desire and my prayer to God for them is for their salvation.
45_10_2: For I testify about them that they have a zeal for God — but not in accordance with knowledge.
45_10_3: For not knowing about God's righteousness — and seeking to establish their own — they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God.
45_10_4: For Christ is the end of the Law for righteousness — to everyone who believes.
45_10_5: For Moses writes that the man who practices the righteousness which is based on Law shall live by that righteousness.
45_10_6: But the righteousness based on faith speaks like this: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?'" (that is, to bring Christ down).
45_10_7: Or, "Who will descend into the abyss?" (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).
45_10_8: But what does it say? "The word is near you — in your mouth and in your heart" — that is, the word of faith which we are preaching.
45_10_9: That if you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead — you will be saved.
45_10_10: For with the heart a person believes, resulting in righteousness — and with the mouth he confesses, resulting in salvation.
45_10_11: For the Scripture says, "Whoever believes in Him will not be put to shame."
45_10_12: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek — for the same Lord is Lord of all, abounding in riches for all who call on Him.
45_10_13: For "whoever will call on the name of the Lord will be saved."
45_10_14: How then will they call on Him in whom they have not believed? And how will they believe in Him whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without a preacher?
45_10_15: And how will they preach unless they are sent? Just as it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news of good things!"
45_10_16: However, they did not all heed the good news. For Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our report?"
45_10_17: So faith comes from hearing — and hearing by the word of Christ.
45_10_18: But I say, surely they have never heard, have they? Indeed they have: "Their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world."
45_10_19: But I say, surely Israel did not know, did they? At the first Moses says: "I will make you jealous by that which is not a nation; by a nation without understanding I will anger you."
45_10_20: And Isaiah is very bold, and says: "I was found by those who did not seek Me; I became manifest to those who did not ask for Me."
45_10_21: But as for Israel He says: "All the day long I have stretched out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people."
45_11_1: I say then — God has not rejected His people, has He? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
45_11_2: God has not rejected His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the passage about Elijah — how he pleads with God against Israel?
45_11_3: "Lord, they have killed Your prophets; they have torn down Your altars; and I alone am left, and they are seeking my life."
45_11_4: But what is the divine response to him? "I have kept for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal."
45_11_5: In the same way then, there has also come to be at the present time a remnant according to God's gracious choice.
45_11_6: But if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works — otherwise grace is no longer grace.
45_11_7: What then? What Israel is seeking, it has not obtained. But those who were chosen obtained it — and the rest were hardened.
45_11_8: Just as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor — eyes to see not, and ears to hear not, down to this very day."
45_11_9: And David says: "Let their table become a snare and a trap, and a stumbling block — and a retribution to them.
45_11_10: Let their eyes be darkened to see not, and bend their backs forever."
45_11_11: I say then — they did not stumble so as to fall, did they? May it never be! But by their transgression salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
45_11_12: Now if their transgression is riches for the world, and their failure is riches for the Gentiles — how much more will their fulfillment be?
45_11_13: But I am speaking to you who are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles, I magnify my ministry —
45_11_14: if somehow I might move to jealousy my fellow countrymen, and save some of them.
45_11_15: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
45_11_16: And if the firstfruits is holy, the lump is also; and if the root is holy, the branches are too.
45_11_17: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them, and became partaker with them of the rich root of the olive tree —
45_11_18: do not be arrogant toward the branches. But if you are arrogant — remember that it is not you who supports the root, but the root supports you.
45_11_19: You will say then, "Branches were broken off, so that I might be grafted in."
45_11_20: Quite right! They were broken off for their unbelief — but you stand by your faith. Do not be conceited, but fear.
45_11_21: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will not spare you either.
45_11_22: Behold then the kindness and severity of God: to those who fell, severity; but to you, God's kindness — if you continue in His kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
45_11_23: And they also, if they do not continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in — for God is able to graft them in again.
45_11_24: For if you were cut off from what is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a cultivated olive tree — how much more will these who are the natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree?
45_11_25: For I do not want you, brothers, to be uninformed of this mystery — so that you will not be wise in your own estimation — that a partial hardening has happened to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in.
45_11_26: And so all Israel will be saved. Just as it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove ungodliness from Jacob.
45_11_27: And this is My covenant with them, when I take away their sins."
45_11_28: From the standpoint of the gospel they are enemies for your sake — but from the standpoint of God's choice, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
45_11_29: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
45_11_30: For just as you once were disobedient to God, but now have been shown mercy because of their disobedience —
45_11_31: so these also now have been disobedient — that because of the mercy shown to you, they also may now be shown mercy.
45_11_32: For God has shut up all in disobedience — so that He may show mercy to all.
45_11_33: Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments — and unfathomable His ways!
45_11_34: For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who became His counselor?
45_11_35: Or who has first given to Him, that it might be paid back to him?
45_11_36: For from Him, and through Him, and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever. Amen.
45_12_1: Therefore, I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God — to present your bodies as a living and holy sacrifice, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
45_12_2: And do not be conformed to this world — but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what the will of God is — that which is good and acceptable and perfect.
45_12_3: For through the grace given to me, I say to everyone among you not to think more highly of himself than he ought to think — but to think so as to have sound judgment, as God has allotted to each a measure of faith.
45_12_4: For just as we have many members in one body, and all the members do not have the same function —
45_12_5: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ — and individually members one of another.
45_12_6: Since we have gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let each exercise them accordingly: if prophecy, according to the proportion of his faith;
45_12_7: if service, in his serving; or he who teaches, in his teaching;
45_12_8: or he who exhorts, in his exhortation; he who gives, with liberality; he who leads, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
45_12_9: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.
45_12_10: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love — give preference to one another in honor.
45_12_11: Not lagging behind in diligence — fervent in spirit, serving the Lord.
45_12_12: Rejoicing in hope, persevering in tribulation, devoted to prayer.
45_12_13: Contributing to the needs of the saints — practicing hospitality.
45_12_14: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
45_12_15: Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
45_12_16: Be of the same mind toward one another. Do not be haughty in mind — but associate with the lowly. Do not be wise in your own estimation.
45_12_17: Never pay back evil for evil to anyone. Respect what is right in the sight of all men.
45_12_18: If possible, so far as it depends on you — be at peace with all men.
45_12_19: Never take your own revenge, beloved — but leave room for the wrath of God. For it is written, "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay," says the Lord.
45_12_20: But "if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink — for in so doing you will heap burning coals on his head."
45_12_21: Do not be overcome by evil — but overcome evil with good.
45_13_1: Every person is to be in subjection to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God — and those which exist are established by God.
45_13_2: Therefore he who resists authority has opposed the ordinance of God — and they who have opposed will receive condemnation upon themselves.
45_13_3: For rulers are not a cause of fear for good behavior, but for evil. Do you want to have no fear of authority? Do what is good — and you will have praise from the same.
45_13_4: For it is a minister of God to you for good. But if you do what is evil, be afraid — for it does not bear the sword for nothing. For it is a minister of God, an avenger who brings wrath on the one who practices evil.
45_13_5: Therefore it is necessary to be in subjection — not only because of wrath, but also for conscience' sake.
45_13_6: For because of this you also pay taxes — for rulers are servants of God, devoting themselves to this very thing.
45_13_7: Render to all what is due them: tax to whom tax is due; custom to whom custom is due; fear to whom fear is due; honor to whom honor is due.
45_13_8: Owe nothing to anyone — except to love one another. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
45_13_9: For this — "You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet," and if there is any other commandment — it is summed up in this saying: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
45_13_10: Love does no wrong to a neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
45_13_11: And do this, knowing the time — that it is already the hour for you to wake from sleep. For now salvation is nearer to us than when we believed.
45_13_12: The night is almost gone, and the day is near. Therefore, let us lay aside the deeds of darkness — and put on the armor of light.
45_13_13: Let us behave properly as in the day — not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and sensuality, not in strife and jealousy.
45_13_14: But put on the Lord Jesus Christ — and make no provision for the flesh, in regard to its lusts.
45_14_1: Now accept the one who is weak in faith — but not for the purpose of passing judgment on his opinions.
45_14_2: One person has faith that he may eat all things — but he who is weak eats vegetables only.
45_14_3: The one who eats is not to regard with contempt the one who does not eat — and the one who does not eat is not to judge the one who eats. For God has accepted him.
45_14_4: Who are you to judge the servant of another? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand — for the Lord is able to make him stand.
45_14_5: One person regards one day above another, another regards every day alike. Each person must be fully convinced in his own mind.
45_14_6: He who observes the day, observes it for the Lord. And he who eats, does so for the Lord — for he gives thanks to God. And he who does not eat, for the Lord he does not eat — and gives thanks to God.
45_14_7: For not one of us lives for himself — and not one dies for himself.
45_14_8: For if we live, we live for the Lord; or if we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.
45_14_9: For to this end Christ died and lived again — that He might be Lord both of the dead and of the living.
45_14_10: But you — why do you judge your brother? Or you again — why do you regard your brother with contempt? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.
45_14_11: For it is written: "As I live, says the Lord — every knee shall bow to Me, and every tongue shall give praise to God."
45_14_12: So then, each one of us will give an account of himself to God.
45_14_13: Therefore let us not judge one another anymore — but rather determine this: not to put an obstacle or a stumbling block in a brother's way.
45_14_14: I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself — but to him who thinks anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.
45_14_15: For if because of food your brother is hurt, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not destroy with your food him for whom Christ died.
45_14_16: Therefore do not let what is for you a good thing be spoken of as evil.
45_14_17: For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking — but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
45_14_18: For the one who serves Christ in this way is acceptable to God — and approved by men.
45_14_19: So then, let us pursue the things which make for peace — and the building up of one another.
45_14_20: Do not tear down the work of God for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean — but they are evil for the man who eats and gives offense.
45_14_21: It is good not to eat meat or to drink wine — or to do anything by which your brother stumbles.
45_14_22: The faith which you have, have as your own conviction before God. Happy is he who does not condemn himself in what he approves.
45_14_23: But he who doubts is condemned if he eats — because his eating is not from faith. And whatever is not from faith is sin.
45_15_1: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength — and not just please ourselves.
45_15_2: Each of us is to please his neighbor for his good — to his edification.
45_15_3: For even Christ did not please Himself — but as it is written: "The reproaches of those who reproached You fell on Me."
45_15_4: For whatever was written in earlier times was written for our instruction — so that through perseverance and the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
45_15_5: Now may the God who gives perseverance and encouragement grant you to be of the same mind with one another, according to Christ Jesus —
45_15_6: that with one accord, you may with one voice glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
45_15_7: Therefore, accept one another, just as Christ also accepted us — to the glory of God.
45_15_8: For I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcision on behalf of the truth of God — to confirm the promises given to the fathers,
45_15_9: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy. Just as it is written: "Therefore I will give praise to You among the Gentiles, and I will sing to Your name."
45_15_10: And again he says: "Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people."
45_15_11: And again: "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles — and let all the peoples praise Him."
45_15_12: And again Isaiah says: "There shall come the root of Jesse, and He who arises to rule over the Gentiles — in Him shall the Gentiles hope."
45_15_13: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing — so that you will abound in hope, by the power of the Holy Spirit.
45_15_14: And concerning you, my brothers, I myself also am convinced that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able also to admonish one another.
45_15_15: But I have written very boldly to you on some points — so as to remind you again, because of the grace that was given me from God,
45_15_16: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles — ministering as a priest the gospel of God, so that my offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
45_15_17: Therefore in Christ Jesus I have found reason for boasting in things pertaining to God.
45_15_18: For I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me — resulting in the obedience of the Gentiles by word and deed,
45_15_19: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit. So that from Jerusalem and round about as far as Illyricum I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
45_15_20: And thus I aspired to preach the gospel — not where Christ was already named — so that I would not build on another man's foundation.
45_15_21: But as it is written: "They who had no news of Him shall see — and they who have not heard shall understand."
45_15_22: For this reason I have often been hindered from coming to you.
45_15_23: But now, with no further place for me in these regions — and since I have had for many years a longing to come to you,
45_15_24: whenever I go to Spain — for I hope to see you in passing, and to be helped on my way there by you, when I have first enjoyed your company for a while.
45_15_25: But now, I am going to Jerusalem — serving the saints.
45_15_26: For Macedonia and Achaia have been pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
45_15_27: Yes, they were pleased to do so — and they are indebted to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they are indebted to minister to them also in material things.
45_15_28: Therefore, when I have finished this — and have put my seal on this fruit of theirs — I will go on by way of you to Spain.
45_15_29: And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
45_15_30: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in your prayers to God for me —
45_15_31: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service for Jerusalem may prove acceptable to the saints.
45_15_32: So that I may come to you in joy by the will of God, and find refreshing rest in your company.
45_15_33: Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
45_16_1: I commend to you our sister Phoebe — who is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea —
45_16_2: that you receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and that you help her in whatever matter she may have need of you. For she herself has also been a helper of many, and of myself as well.
45_16_3: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
45_16_4: who for my life risked their own necks — to whom not only do I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.
45_16_5: Also greet the church that is in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruits to Christ from Asia.
45_16_6: Greet Mary, who has worked hard for you.
45_16_7: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners — who are outstanding among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
45_16_8: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
45_16_9: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ — and Stachys my beloved.
45_16_10: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.
45_16_11: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
45_16_12: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, workers in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who has worked hard in the Lord.
45_16_13: Greet Rufus, a choice man in the Lord — also his mother and mine.
45_16_14: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
45_16_15: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
45_16_16: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
45_16_17: Now I urge you, brothers, keep your eye on those who cause dissensions and hindrances contrary to the teaching which you learned — and turn away from them.
45_16_18: For such men are slaves not of our Lord Christ, but of their own appetites — and by their smooth and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.
45_16_19: For the report of your obedience has reached to all. Therefore I am rejoicing over you. But I want you to be wise in what is good — and innocent in what is evil.
45_16_20: And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
45_16_21: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you — and so do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.
45_16_22: I, Tertius, who write this letter, greet you in the Lord.
45_16_23: Gaius, host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you — and Quartus, the brother.
45_16_24: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
45_16_25: Now to Him who is able to establish you, according to my gospel and the preaching of Jesus Christ — according to the revelation of the mystery which has been kept secret for long ages past,
45_16_26: but now is manifested — and by the Scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the eternal God, has been made known to all the nations, leading to obedience of faith —
45_16_27: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ — to Him be the glory forever. Amen.
46_1_1: Paul, called as an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother —
46_1_2: to the church of God which is at Corinth — to those who have been sanctified in Christ Jesus, called as saints, with all who in every place call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
46_1_3: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
46_1_4: I thank my God always concerning you — for the grace of God which was given you in Christ Jesus,
46_1_5: that in everything you were enriched in Him — in all speech and all knowledge,
46_1_6: even as the testimony concerning Christ was confirmed in you,
46_1_7: so that you are not lacking in any gift, awaiting eagerly the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
46_1_8: Who will also confirm you to the end — blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
46_1_9: God is faithful — through whom you were called into fellowship with His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
46_1_10: Now I urge you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ — that you all agree, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be made complete in the same mind and in the same judgment.
46_1_11: For I have been informed concerning you, my brothers, by Chloe's people — that there are quarrels among you.
46_1_12: Now I mean this — that each one of you is saying, "I am of Paul," and "I of Apollos," and "I of Cephas," and "I of Christ."
46_1_13: Has Christ been divided? Paul was not crucified for you, was he? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
46_1_14: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius —
46_1_15: so that no one would say you were baptized in my name.
46_1_16: Now I did baptize also the household of Stephanas. Beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized any other.
46_1_17: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel — not in cleverness of speech, so that the cross of Christ would not be made void.
46_1_18: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing — but to us who are being saved, it is the power of God.
46_1_19: For it is written: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the cleverness of the clever I will set aside."
46_1_20: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
46_1_21: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not come to know God — God was well-pleased through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe.
46_1_22: For indeed Jews ask for signs, and Greeks search for wisdom —
46_1_23: but we preach Christ crucified — to Jews a stumbling block, and to Gentiles foolishness.
46_1_24: But to those who are the called — both Jews and Greeks — Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.
46_1_25: Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men — and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
46_1_26: For consider your calling, brothers — that there were not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble.
46_1_27: But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to shame the wise. And God has chosen the weak things of the world to shame the things which are strong.
46_1_28: And the base things of the world, and the despised, God has chosen — the things that are not, so that He may nullify the things that are.
46_1_29: So that no man may boast before God.
46_1_30: But by His doing you are in Christ Jesus — who became to us wisdom from God, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption.
46_1_31: So that, just as it is written, "Let him who boasts, boast in the Lord."
46_2_1: And when I came to you, brothers, I did not come with superiority of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.
46_2_2: For I determined to know nothing among you — except Jesus Christ, and Him crucified.
46_2_3: And I was with you in weakness — and in fear, and in much trembling.
46_2_4: And my message and my preaching were not in persuasive words of wisdom — but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
46_2_5: so that your faith would not rest on the wisdom of men — but on the power of God.
46_2_6: Yet we do speak wisdom among those who are mature — a wisdom, however, not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are passing away.
46_2_7: But we speak God's wisdom in a mystery — the hidden wisdom which God predestined before the ages to our glory.
46_2_8: The wisdom which none of the rulers of this age has understood — for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
46_2_9: But just as it is written: "Things which eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and which have not entered the heart of man — all that God has prepared for those who love Him."
46_2_10: For to us God revealed them through the Spirit. For the Spirit searches all things — even the depths of God.
46_2_11: For who among men knows the thoughts of a man, except the spirit of the man, which is in him? Even so, the thoughts of God no one knows except the Spirit of God.
46_2_12: Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God — so that we may know the things freely given to us by God.
46_2_13: Which things we also speak — not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Spirit, combining spiritual thoughts with spiritual words.
46_2_14: But a natural man does not accept the things of the Spirit of God — for they are foolishness to him. And he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually appraised.
46_2_15: But he who is spiritual appraises all things — yet he himself is appraised by no one.
46_2_16: For "who has known the mind of the Lord, that he will instruct Him?" But we have the mind of Christ.
46_3_1: And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual men — but as to men of flesh, as to infants in Christ.
46_3_2: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food — for you were not yet able to receive it. Indeed, even now you are not yet able.
46_3_3: For you are still fleshly. For where there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not fleshly — and are you not walking like mere men?
46_3_4: For when one says, "I am of Paul," and another, "I am of Apollos," are you not mere men?
46_3_5: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed — even as the Lord gave opportunity to each one.
46_3_6: I planted, Apollos watered — but God was causing the growth.
46_3_7: So then neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything — but God who causes the growth.
46_3_8: Now he who plants and he who waters are one. But each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
46_3_9: For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's field — God's building.
46_3_10: According to the grace of God which was given to me, like a wise master builder I laid a foundation — and another is building on it. But each man must be careful how he builds on it.
46_3_11: For no man can lay a foundation other than the one which is laid — which is Jesus Christ.
46_3_12: Now if any man builds on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw —
46_3_13: each man's work will become evident. For the day will show it — because it is to be revealed with fire — and the fire itself will test the quality of each man's work.
46_3_14: If any man's work which he has built on it remains, he will receive a reward.
46_3_15: If any man's work is burned up, he will suffer loss — but he himself will be saved, yet so as through fire.
46_3_16: Do you not know that you are a temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
46_3_17: If any man destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him — for the temple of God is holy, and that is what you are.
46_3_18: Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you thinks that he is wise in this age, let him become foolish, so that he may become wise.
46_3_19: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness before God. For it is written: "He is the one who catches the wise in their craftiness."
46_3_20: And again: "The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise — that they are useless."
46_3_21: So then let no one boast in men. For all things belong to you —
46_3_22: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas, or the world or life or death, or things present or things to come — all things belong to you.
46_3_23: And you belong to Christ — and Christ belongs to God.
46_4_1: Let a man regard us in this manner — as servants of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.
46_4_2: In this case, moreover, it is required of stewards that one be found trustworthy.
46_4_3: But to me it is a very small thing that I may be examined by you, or by any human court. In fact, I do not even examine myself.
46_4_4: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, yet I am not by this acquitted. But the one who examines me is the Lord.
46_4_5: Therefore do not go on passing judgment before the time — but wait until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the things hidden in the darkness, and disclose the motives of men's hearts. Then each man's praise will come to him from God.
46_4_6: Now these things, brothers, I have figuratively applied to myself and Apollos for your sakes — so that in us you may learn not to exceed what is written, in order that no one of you will become arrogant in behalf of one against the other.
46_4_7: For who regards you as superior? And what do you have that you did not receive? But if you did receive it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
46_4_8: You are already filled, you have already become rich, you have become kings without us — and indeed, I wish that you had become kings, so that we also might reign with you.
46_4_9: For, I think, God has exhibited us apostles last of all, as men condemned to death — because we have become a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to men.
46_4_10: We are fools for Christ's sake — but you are prudent in Christ. We are weak — but you are strong. You are distinguished — but we are without honor.
46_4_11: To this present hour we are both hungry and thirsty — and we are poorly clothed and roughly treated, and homeless.
46_4_12: And we toil, working with our own hands. When we are reviled, we bless. When we are persecuted, we endure.
46_4_13: When we are slandered, we try to conciliate. We have become as the scum of the world, the dregs of all things, even until now.
46_4_14: I do not write these things to shame you — but to admonish you as my beloved children.
46_4_15: For if you were to have countless tutors in Christ, yet you would not have many fathers — for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
46_4_16: Therefore I exhort you — be imitators of me.
46_4_17: For this reason I have sent to you Timothy — who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways which are in Christ — just as I teach everywhere in every church.
46_4_18: Now some have become arrogant — as though I were not coming to you.
46_4_19: But I will come to you soon — if the Lord wills — and I shall find out, not the words of those who are arrogant, but their power.
46_4_20: For the kingdom of God does not consist in words — but in power.
46_4_21: What do you desire? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?
46_5_1: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you — and immorality of such a kind as does not exist even among the Gentiles, that someone has his father's wife.
46_5_2: And you have become arrogant — and have not mourned instead, so that the one who had done this deed would be removed from your midst.
46_5_3: For I, on my part — though absent in body but present in spirit — have already judged him who has so committed this, as though I were present.
46_5_4: In the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are assembled, and I with you in spirit — with the power of our Lord Jesus —
46_5_5: I have decided to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of his flesh, so that his spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
46_5_6: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump of dough?
46_5_7: Clean out the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump — just as you are in fact unleavened. For Christ our Passover also has been sacrificed.
46_5_8: Therefore let us celebrate the feast — not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
46_5_9: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people —
46_5_10: I did not at all mean with the sexually immoral people of this world — or with the covetous and swindlers, or with idolaters. For then you would have to go out of the world.
46_5_11: But actually, I wrote to you not to associate with any so-called brother, if he is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or a swindler — not even to eat with such a one.
46_5_12: For what have I to do with judging outsiders? Do you not judge those who are within the church?
46_5_13: But those who are outside, God judges. "Remove the wicked man from among yourselves."
46_6_1: Does any one of you, when he has a case against his neighbor, dare to go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
46_6_2: Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? If the world is judged by you, are you not competent to constitute the smallest law courts?
46_6_3: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more matters of this life?
46_6_4: So if you have law courts dealing with matters of this life, do you appoint them as judges who are of no account in the church?
46_6_5: I say this to your shame. Is it so that there is not among you one wise man who will be able to decide between his brothers?
46_6_6: But brother goes to law with brother — and that before unbelievers!
46_6_7: Actually, then, it is already a defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
46_6_8: On the contrary, you yourselves wrong and defraud — and even your brothers!
46_6_9: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived. Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor those who practice homosexuality,
46_6_10: nor thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.
46_6_11: And such were some of you. But you were washed; but you were sanctified; but you were justified — in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God.
46_6_12: All things are lawful for me — but not all things are profitable. All things are lawful for me — but I will not be mastered by anything.
46_6_13: Food is for the stomach, and the stomach is for food — but God will do away with both of them. Yet the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord — and the Lord is for the body.
46_6_14: Now God has not only raised the Lord — but will also raise us up through His power.
46_6_15: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take away the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
46_6_16: Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For He says, "The two shall become one flesh."
46_6_17: But the one who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with Him.
46_6_18: Flee sexual immorality. Every other sin that a man commits is outside the body — but the immoral man sins against his own body.
46_6_19: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you — whom you have from God? And you are not your own,
46_6_20: for you have been bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.
46_7_1: Now concerning the things about which you wrote — it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
46_7_2: But because of immoralities, each man is to have his own wife — and each woman is to have her own husband.
46_7_3: The husband must fulfill his duty to his wife — and likewise also the wife to her husband.
46_7_4: The wife does not have authority over her own body — but the husband does. And likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body — but the wife does.
46_7_5: Stop depriving one another, except by agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer — and come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
46_7_6: But this I say by way of concession, not of command.
46_7_7: Yet I wish that all men were even as I myself am. However, each man has his own gift from God — one in this manner, and another in that.
46_7_8: But I say to the unmarried and to widows that it is good for them if they remain even as I.
46_7_9: But if they do not have self-control, let them marry — for it is better to marry than to burn with passion.
46_7_10: But to the married I give instructions — not I, but the Lord — that the wife should not leave her husband.
46_7_11: But if she does leave, she must remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband. And the husband should not divorce his wife.
46_7_12: But to the rest I say, not the Lord, that if any brother has a wife who is an unbeliever, and she consents to live with him — he must not divorce her.
46_7_13: And a woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to live with her — she must not divorce her husband.
46_7_14: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his wife — and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise, your children are unclean — but now they are holy.
46_7_15: Yet if the unbelieving one leaves, let him leave. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases — but God has called us to peace.
46_7_16: For how do you know, O wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, O husband, whether you will save your wife?
46_7_17: Only, as the Lord has assigned to each one — as God has called each — in this manner let him walk. And so I direct in all the churches.
46_7_18: Was any man called when he was already circumcised? He is not to become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? He is not to be circumcised.
46_7_19: Circumcision is nothing — and uncircumcision is nothing. But what matters is the keeping of the commandments of God.
46_7_20: Each man must remain in that condition in which he was called.
46_7_21: Were you called while a slave? Do not worry about it — but if you are able also to become free, rather do that.
46_7_22: For he who was called in the Lord while a slave is the Lord's freedman — likewise he who was called while free is Christ's slave.
46_7_23: You were bought with a price. Do not become slaves of men.
46_7_24: Brothers, each one is to remain with God in that condition in which he was called.
46_7_25: Now concerning virgins, I have no command of the Lord — but I give an opinion as one who by the mercy of the Lord is trustworthy.
46_7_26: I think then that this is good in view of the present distress — that it is good for a man to remain as he is.
46_7_27: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
46_7_28: But if you marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have trouble in this life — and I am trying to spare you.
46_7_29: But this I say, brothers — the time has been shortened, so that from now on, those who have wives should be as though they had none.
46_7_30: And those who weep, as though they did not weep — and those who rejoice, as though they did not rejoice — and those who buy, as though they did not possess.
46_7_31: And those who use the world, as though they did not make full use of it. For the form of this world is passing away.
46_7_32: But I want you to be free from concern. One who is unmarried is concerned about the things of the Lord — how he may please the Lord.
46_7_33: But one who is married is concerned about the things of the world — how he may please his wife.
46_7_34: And his interests are divided. The woman who is unmarried, and the virgin, is concerned about the things of the Lord — that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But one who is married is concerned about the things of the world — how she may please her husband.
46_7_35: This I say for your own benefit — not to put a restraint upon you, but to promote what is appropriate, and to secure undistracted devotion to the Lord.
46_7_36: But if any man thinks that he is acting unbecomingly toward his virgin daughter, if she is past her youth — and if it must be so — let him do what he wishes; he does not sin. Let her marry.
46_7_37: But he who stands firm in his heart, being under no constraint, but has authority over his own will, and has decided this in his own heart — to keep his own virgin daughter, he will do well.
46_7_38: So then both he who gives his own virgin daughter in marriage does well, and he who does not give her in marriage will do better.
46_7_39: A wife is bound as long as her husband lives — but if her husband is dead, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord.
46_7_40: But in my opinion she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I also have the Spirit of God.
46_8_1: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols — we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge makes arrogant — but love edifies.
46_8_2: If anyone supposes that he knows anything, he has not yet known as he ought to know.
46_8_3: But if anyone loves God, he is known by Him.
46_8_4: Therefore, concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that there is no such thing as an idol in the world — and that there is no God but one.
46_8_5: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth — as indeed there are many gods and many lords —
46_8_6: yet for us there is but one God, the Father — from whom are all things, and we exist for Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ — through whom are all things, and we exist through Him.
46_8_7: However, not all men have this knowledge. But some, being accustomed to the idol until now, eat food as if it were sacrificed to an idol — and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
46_8_8: But food will not commend us to God — we are neither the worse if we do not eat, nor the better if we do eat.
46_8_9: But take care that this liberty of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.
46_8_10: For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, dining in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, if he is weak, be strengthened to eat things sacrificed to idols?
46_8_11: For through your knowledge he who is weak is ruined — the brother for whose sake Christ died.
46_8_12: And so, by sinning against the brothers and wounding their conscience when it is weak, you sin against Christ.
46_8_13: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again — so that I will not cause my brother to stumble.
46_9_1: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
46_9_2: If to others I am not an apostle — at least I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
46_9_3: My defense to those who examine me is this:
46_9_4: Do we not have a right to eat and drink?
46_9_5: Do we not have a right to take along a believing wife — even as the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
46_9_6: Or do only Barnabas and I not have a right to refrain from working?
46_9_7: Who at any time serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat the fruit of it? Or who tends a flock and does not use the milk of the flock?
46_9_8: I am not speaking these things according to human judgment, am I? Or does not the Law also say these things?
46_9_9: For it is written in the Law of Moses: "You shall not muzzle the ox while it is threshing." God is not concerned about oxen, is He?
46_9_10: Or is He speaking altogether for our sake? Yes, for our sake it was written — because the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the thresher to thresh in hope of sharing the crops.
46_9_11: If we sowed spiritual things in you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?
46_9_12: If others share the right over you — do we not more? Nevertheless, we did not use this right — but we endure all things, so that we will cause no hindrance to the gospel of Christ.
46_9_13: Do you not know that those who perform sacred services eat the food of the temple — and those who attend regularly to the altar have their share with the altar?
46_9_14: So also the Lord directed those who proclaim the gospel to get their living from the gospel.
46_9_15: But I have used none of these things. And I am not writing these things so that it will be done so in my case — for it would be better for me to die than have any man make my boast an empty one.
46_9_16: For if I preach the gospel, I have nothing to boast of — for I am under compulsion. For woe is me if I do not preach the gospel.
46_9_17: For if I do this voluntarily, I have a reward. But if against my will, I have a stewardship entrusted to me.
46_9_18: What then is my reward? That, when I preach the gospel, I may offer the gospel without charge — so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel.
46_9_19: For though I am free from all men, I have made myself a slave to all — so that I may win more.
46_9_20: To the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews. To those who are under the Law, as under the Law (though not being myself under the Law) — so that I might win those who are under the Law.
46_9_21: To those who are without the Law, as without the Law (though not being without the Law of God, but under the law of Christ) — so that I might win those who are without the Law.
46_9_22: To the weak I became weak, that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all men — so that I may by all means save some.
46_9_23: I do all things for the sake of the gospel — so that I may become a fellow partaker of it.
46_9_24: Do you not know that those who run in a race all run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may win.
46_9_25: Everyone who competes in the games exercises self-control in all things. They do it to receive a perishable wreath — but we, an imperishable.
46_9_26: Therefore I run in such a way as not without aim. I box in such a way as not beating the air.
46_9_27: But I discipline my body — and make it my slave, so that, after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
46_10_1: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud — and all passed through the sea;
46_10_2: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
46_10_3: And all ate the same spiritual food.
46_10_4: And all drank the same spiritual drink — for they were drinking from a spiritual rock which followed them. And the rock was Christ.
46_10_5: Nevertheless, with most of them God was not well-pleased — for they were laid low in the wilderness.
46_10_6: Now these things happened as examples for us — so that we would not crave evil things, as they also craved.
46_10_7: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written, "The people sat down to eat and drink, and stood up to play."
46_10_8: Nor let us act immorally, as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
46_10_9: Nor let us put the Lord to the test, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the serpents.
46_10_10: Nor grumble, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the destroyer.
46_10_11: Now these things happened to them as an example, and they were written for our instruction — upon whom the ends of the ages have come.
46_10_12: Therefore let him who thinks he stands take heed that he does not fall.
46_10_13: No temptation has overtaken you but such as is common to man. And God is faithful — who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able. But with the temptation will provide the way of escape also, so that you will be able to endure it.
46_10_14: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
46_10_15: I speak as to wise men. You judge what I say.
46_10_16: Is not the cup of blessing which we bless a sharing in the blood of Christ? Is not the bread which we break a sharing in the body of Christ?
46_10_17: Since there is one bread, we who are many are one body — for we all partake of the one bread.
46_10_18: Look at the nation Israel. Are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers in the altar?
46_10_19: What do I mean then? That a thing sacrificed to idols is anything? Or that an idol is anything?
46_10_20: No — but I say that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons, and not to God. And I do not want you to become sharers in demons.
46_10_21: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
46_10_22: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? We are not stronger than He, are we?
46_10_23: All things are lawful — but not all things are profitable. All things are lawful — but not all things edify.
46_10_24: Let no one seek his own good, but that of his neighbor.
46_10_25: Eat anything that is sold in the meat market — without asking questions for conscience' sake.
46_10_26: For "the earth is the Lord's, and all it contains."
46_10_27: If one of the unbelievers invites you, and you wish to go — eat anything that is set before you, without asking questions for conscience' sake.
46_10_28: But if anyone says to you, "This is meat sacrificed to idols" — do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you, and for conscience' sake.
46_10_29: I mean not your own conscience, but the other man's. For why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?
46_10_30: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I slandered concerning that for which I give thanks?
46_10_31: Therefore, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do — do all to the glory of God.
46_10_32: Give no offense — either to Jews, or to Greeks, or to the church of God.
46_10_33: Just as I also please all men in all things — not seeking my own profit, but the profit of the many, so that they may be saved.
46_11_1: Be imitators of me — just as I also am of Christ.
46_11_2: Now I praise you because you remember me in everything — and hold firmly to the traditions, just as I delivered them to you.
46_11_3: But I want you to understand that Christ is the head of every man — and the man is the head of a woman, and God is the head of Christ.
46_11_4: Every man who has something on his head while praying or prophesying disgraces his head.
46_11_5: But every woman who has her head uncovered while praying or prophesying disgraces her head — for she is one and the same as the woman whose head is shaved.
46_11_6: For if a woman does not cover her head, let her also have her hair cut off. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, let her cover her head.
46_11_7: For a man ought not to have his head covered, since he is the image and glory of God — but the woman is the glory of man.
46_11_8: For man does not originate from woman — but woman from man.
46_11_9: For indeed man was not created for the woman's sake, but woman for the man's sake.
46_11_10: Therefore the woman ought to have a symbol of authority on her head, because of the angels.
46_11_11: However, in the Lord, neither is woman independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.
46_11_12: For as the woman originates from the man, so also the man has his birth through the woman — and all things originate from God.
46_11_13: Judge for yourselves — is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
46_11_14: Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a dishonor to him?
46_11_15: But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her — for her hair is given to her as a covering.
46_11_16: But if anyone seems to be contentious — we have no other practice, nor have the churches of God.
46_11_17: But in giving this instruction, I do not praise you — because you come together not for the better, but for the worse.
46_11_18: For, in the first place, when you come together as a church, I hear that divisions exist among you — and in part I believe it.
46_11_19: For there must also be factions among you — so that those who are approved may become evident among you.
46_11_20: Therefore when you meet together — it is not to eat the Lord's Supper.
46_11_21: For in your eating, each one takes his own supper first — and one is hungry, and another is drunk.
46_11_22: What! Do you not have houses in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God, and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I will not praise you.
46_11_23: For I received from the Lord that which I also delivered to you — that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which He was betrayed, took bread.
46_11_24: And when He had given thanks, He broke it and said: "This is My body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of Me."
46_11_25: In the same way He took the cup also after supper, saying: "This cup is the new covenant in My blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me."
46_11_26: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup — you proclaim the Lord's death until He comes.
46_11_27: Therefore whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner — shall be guilty of the body and the blood of the Lord.
46_11_28: But a man must examine himself — and in so doing he is to eat of the bread and drink of the cup.
46_11_29: For he who eats and drinks, eats and drinks judgment to himself if he does not judge the body rightly.
46_11_30: For this reason many among you are weak and sick — and a number sleep.
46_11_31: But if we judged ourselves rightly, we would not be judged.
46_11_32: But when we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord — so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
46_11_33: So then, my brothers, when you come together to eat — wait for one another.
46_11_34: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home — so that you will not come together for judgment. The remaining matters I will arrange when I come.
46_12_1: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers — I do not want you to be unaware.
46_12_2: You know that when you were pagans, you were led astray to the mute idols, however you were led.
46_12_3: Therefore I make known to you, that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed." And no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.
46_12_4: Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit.
46_12_5: And there are varieties of ministries — and the same Lord.
46_12_6: And there are varieties of effects — but the same God who works all things in all persons.
46_12_7: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
46_12_8: For to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit — and to another the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit.
46_12_9: To another faith by the same Spirit — and to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit.
46_12_10: And to another the effecting of miracles — and to another prophecy, and to another the distinguishing of spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, and to another the interpretation of tongues.
46_12_11: But one and the same Spirit works all these things — distributing to each one individually just as He wills.
46_12_12: For even as the body is one and yet has many members, and all the members of the body, though they are many, are one body — so also is Christ.
46_12_13: For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body — whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free — and we were all made to drink of one Spirit.
46_12_14: For the body is not one member, but many.
46_12_15: If the foot says, "Because I am not a hand, I am not a part of the body," it is not for this reason any the less a part of the body.
46_12_16: And if the ear says, "Because I am not an eye, I am not a part of the body," it is not for this reason any the less a part of the body.
46_12_17: If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
46_12_18: But now God has placed the members, each one of them, in the body, just as He desired.
46_12_19: If they were all one member, where would the body be?
46_12_20: But now there are many members — but one body.
46_12_21: And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you." Or again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."
46_12_22: On the contrary, it is much truer that the members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
46_12_23: And those members of the body which we deem less honorable, on these we bestow more abundant honor — and our less presentable members become much more presentable.
46_12_24: Whereas our more presentable members have no need of it. But God has so composed the body, giving more abundant honor to that member which lacked.
46_12_25: So that there may be no division in the body — but that the members may have the same care for one another.
46_12_26: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. If one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
46_12_27: Now you are Christ's body — and individually members of it.
46_12_28: And God has appointed in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers; then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, various kinds of tongues.
46_12_29: All are not apostles, are they? All are not prophets, are they? All are not teachers, are they? All are not workers of miracles, are they?
46_12_30: All do not have gifts of healings, do they? All do not speak with tongues, do they? All do not interpret, do they?
46_12_31: But earnestly desire the greater gifts. And I show you a still more excellent way.
46_13_1: If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels — but do not have love, I have become a noisy gong, or a clanging cymbal.
46_13_2: And if I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge — and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
46_13_3: And if I give all my possessions to feed the poor, and if I surrender my body to be burned — but do not have love, it profits me nothing.
46_13_4: Love is patient. Love is kind. Love is not jealous. Love does not brag, and is not arrogant.
46_13_5: Love does not act unbecomingly; it does not seek its own; it is not provoked; it does not take into account a wrong suffered.
46_13_6: Love does not rejoice in unrighteousness — but rejoices with the truth.
46_13_7: Love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
46_13_8: Love never fails. But if there are gifts of prophecy, they will be done away. If there are tongues, they will cease. If there is knowledge, it will be done away.
46_13_9: For we know in part — and we prophesy in part.
46_13_10: But when the perfect comes, the partial will be done away.
46_13_11: When I was a child, I used to speak as a child, think as a child, reason as a child. When I became a man, I did away with childish things.
46_13_12: For now we see in a mirror dimly — but then face to face. Now I know in part — but then I will know fully, just as I also have been fully known.
46_13_13: But now faith, hope, love abide — these three. But the greatest of these is love.
46_14_1: Pursue love. Yet desire earnestly spiritual gifts — but especially that you may prophesy.
46_14_2: For one who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God — for no one understands; but in his spirit he speaks mysteries.
46_14_3: But one who prophesies speaks to men for edification, and exhortation, and consolation.
46_14_4: One who speaks in a tongue edifies himself — but one who prophesies edifies the church.
46_14_5: Now I wish that you all spoke in tongues, but even more that you would prophesy. And greater is one who prophesies than one who speaks in tongues — unless he interprets, so that the church may receive edifying.
46_14_6: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you — unless I speak to you either by way of revelation or of knowledge or of prophecy or of teaching?
46_14_7: Yet even lifeless things, either flute or harp, in producing a sound — if they do not produce a distinction in the tones, how will it be known what is played on the flute or on the harp?
46_14_8: For if the bugle produces an indistinct sound, who will prepare himself for battle?
46_14_9: So also you, unless you utter by the tongue speech that is clear, how will it be known what is spoken? For you will be speaking into the air.
46_14_10: There are, perhaps, a great many kinds of languages in the world — and no kind is without meaning.
46_14_11: If then I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be to the one who speaks a barbarian — and the one who speaks will be a barbarian to me.
46_14_12: So also you, since you are zealous of spiritual gifts — seek to abound for the edification of the church.
46_14_13: Therefore let one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
46_14_14: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays — but my mind is unfruitful.
46_14_15: What is the outcome then? I will pray with the spirit — and I will pray with the mind also. I will sing with the spirit — and I will sing with the mind also.
46_14_16: Otherwise if you bless in the spirit only, how will the one who fills the place of the ungifted say the "Amen" at your giving of thanks — since he does not know what you are saying?
46_14_17: For you are giving thanks well enough — but the other person is not edified.
46_14_18: I thank God, I speak in tongues more than you all.
46_14_19: However, in the church I desire to speak five words with my mind — so that I may instruct others also — rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.
46_14_20: Brothers, do not be children in your thinking. Yet in evil be infants — but in your thinking be mature.
46_14_21: In the Law it is written: "By men of strange tongues and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people — and even so, they will not listen to Me," says the Lord.
46_14_22: So then tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe but to unbelievers — but prophecy is for a sign, not to unbelievers but to those who believe.
46_14_23: Therefore if the whole church assembles together and all speak in tongues — and ungifted men or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are mad?
46_14_24: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an ungifted man enters — he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all.
46_14_25: The secrets of his heart are disclosed — and so he will fall on his face and worship God, declaring that God is certainly among you.
46_14_26: What is the outcome then, brothers? When you assemble — each one has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
46_14_27: If anyone speaks in a tongue, it should be by two or at the most three — and each in turn, and one must interpret.
46_14_28: But if there is no interpreter, he must keep silent in the church — and let him speak to himself, and to God.
46_14_29: And let two or three prophets speak — and let the others pass judgment.
46_14_30: But if a revelation is made to another who is seated, the first one must keep silent.
46_14_31: For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn — and all may be exhorted.
46_14_32: And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
46_14_33: For God is not a God of confusion, but of peace — as in all the churches of the saints.
46_14_34: The women are to keep silent in the churches. For they are not permitted to speak — but are to subject themselves, just as the Law also says.
46_14_35: And if they desire to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home — for it is improper for a woman to speak in church.
46_14_36: Was it from you that the word of God first went forth? Or has it come to you only?
46_14_37: If anyone thinks he is a prophet, or spiritual, let him recognize that the things which I write to you are the Lord's commandment.
46_14_38: But if anyone does not recognize this, he is not recognized.
46_14_39: Therefore, my brothers, desire earnestly to prophesy — and do not forbid to speak in tongues.
46_14_40: But all things must be done properly and in an orderly manner.
46_15_1: Now I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I preached to you — which also you received, in which also you stand,
46_15_2: by which also you are saved, if you hold fast the word which I preached to you — unless you believed in vain.
46_15_3: For I delivered to you, as of first importance, what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
46_15_4: and that He was buried, and that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.
46_15_5: And that He appeared to Cephas — then to the twelve.
46_15_6: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom remain until now — but some have fallen asleep.
46_15_7: Then He appeared to James — then to all the apostles.
46_15_8: And last of all, as to one untimely born, He appeared to me also.
46_15_9: For I am the least of the apostles, and not fit to be called an apostle — because I persecuted the church of God.
46_15_10: But by the grace of God I am what I am. And His grace toward me did not prove vain — but I labored even more than all of them. Yet not I, but the grace of God with me.
46_15_11: Whether then it was I or they, so we preach — and so you believed.
46_15_12: Now if Christ is preached, that He has been raised from the dead — how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
46_15_13: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, not even Christ has been raised.
46_15_14: And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is vain — your faith also is vain.
46_15_15: Moreover we are even found to be false witnesses of God — because we testified against God that He raised Christ, whom He did not raise, if in fact the dead are not raised.
46_15_16: For if the dead are not raised — not even Christ has been raised.
46_15_17: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is worthless. You are still in your sins.
46_15_18: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
46_15_19: If we have hoped in Christ in this life only, we are of all men most to be pitied.
46_15_20: But now Christ has been raised from the dead — the firstfruits of those who are asleep.
46_15_21: For since by a man came death, by a man also came the resurrection of the dead.
46_15_22: For as in Adam all die — so also in Christ all will be made alive.
46_15_23: But each in his own order — Christ the firstfruits, after that those who are Christ's at His coming.
46_15_24: Then comes the end — when He hands over the kingdom to the God and Father, when He has abolished all rule and all authority and power.
46_15_25: For He must reign — until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
46_15_26: The last enemy that will be abolished is death.
46_15_27: For "He has put all things in subjection under His feet." But when He says, "All things are put in subjection," it is evident that He is excepted who put all things in subjection to Him.
46_15_28: When all things are subjected to Him, then the Son Himself also will be subjected to the One who subjected all things to Him — so that God may be all in all.
46_15_29: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized for them?
46_15_30: And why are we also in danger every hour?
46_15_31: I affirm, brothers, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
46_15_32: If from human motives I fought with wild beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, "Let us eat and drink — for tomorrow we die."
46_15_33: Do not be deceived: bad company corrupts good morals.
46_15_34: Become sober-minded as you ought, and stop sinning. For some have no knowledge of God — I speak this to your shame.
46_15_35: But someone will say, "How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?"
46_15_36: You fool! That which you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
46_15_37: And that which you sow, you do not sow the body which is to be — but a bare grain, perhaps of wheat or of something else.
46_15_38: But God gives it a body just as He wished — and to each of the seeds a body of its own.
46_15_39: All flesh is not the same flesh — but there is one flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another flesh of birds, and another of fish.
46_15_40: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the glory of the heavenly is one, and the glory of the earthly is another.
46_15_41: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars — for star differs from star in glory.
46_15_42: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown a perishable body — it is raised an imperishable body.
46_15_43: It is sown in dishonor — it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness — it is raised in power.
46_15_44: It is sown a natural body — it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
46_15_45: So also it is written: "The first man, Adam, became a living soul." The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
46_15_46: However, the spiritual is not first, but the natural — then the spiritual.
46_15_47: The first man is from the earth, earthy. The second man is from heaven.
46_15_48: As is the earthy, so also are those who are earthy. And as is the heavenly, so also are those who are heavenly.
46_15_49: And just as we have borne the image of the earthy — we will also bear the image of the heavenly.
46_15_50: Now I say this, brothers — that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God. Nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
46_15_51: Behold, I tell you a mystery — we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed.
46_15_52: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet — for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
46_15_53: For this perishable must put on the imperishable — and this mortal must put on immortality.
46_15_54: But when this perishable will have put on the imperishable, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then will come about the saying that is written: "Death is swallowed up in victory."
46_15_55: "O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?"
46_15_56: The sting of death is sin — and the power of sin is the law.
46_15_57: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
46_15_58: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord — knowing that your toil is not in vain in the Lord.
46_16_1: Now concerning the collection for the saints — as I directed the churches of Galatia, so do you also.
46_16_2: On the first day of every week, each one of you is to put aside and save, as he may prosper — so that no collections be made when I come.
46_16_3: When I arrive, whomever you may approve, I will send them with letters to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
46_16_4: And if it is fitting for me to go also, they will go with me.
46_16_5: But I will come to you after I go through Macedonia — for I am going through Macedonia.
46_16_6: And perhaps I will stay with you, or even spend the winter — so that you may send me on my way wherever I may go.
46_16_7: For I do not wish to see you now just in passing — for I hope to remain with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
46_16_8: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost.
