44_16_12: And from there to Philippi, which is a leading city of the district of Macedonia, a Roman colony. And we were staying in this city for some days.
44_16_13: And on the Sabbath day we went outside the gate to a riverside — where we were supposing that there would be a place of prayer. And we sat down and began speaking to the women who had assembled.
44_16_14: And a certain woman named Lydia, from the city of Thyatira, a seller of purple fabrics, a worshiper of God, was listening — and the Lord opened her heart to respond to the things spoken by Paul.
44_16_15: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, saying, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay." And she prevailed upon us.
44_16_16: And it happened, that as we were going to the place of prayer, a certain slave-girl having a spirit of divination met us — who was bringing her masters much profit by fortunetelling.
44_16_17: Following after Paul and us, she kept crying out, saying, "These men are bondservants of the Most High God — who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation."
44_16_18: And she continued doing this for many days. But Paul was greatly annoyed, and turned and said to the spirit, "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!" And it came out at that very moment.
44_16_19: But when her masters saw that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the market place before the authorities.
44_16_20: And when they had brought them to the chief magistrates, they said: "These men, being Jews, are throwing our city into confusion —
44_16_21: and are proclaiming customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans."
44_16_22: And the crowd rose up together against them — and the chief magistrates tore their robes off them, and proceeded to order them to be beaten with rods.
44_16_23: And when they had inflicted many blows upon them, they threw them into prison — commanding the jailer to guard them securely.
44_16_24: And he, having received such a command, threw them into the inner prison — and fastened their feet in the stocks.
44_16_25: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns of praise to God — and the prisoners were listening to them.
44_16_26: And suddenly there came a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison house were shaken. And immediately all the doors were opened — and everyone's chains were unfastened.
44_16_27: And when the jailer had been roused out of sleep, and had seen the prison doors opened, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself — supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
44_16_28: But Paul cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Do not harm yourself, for we are all here!"
44_16_29: And he called for lights and rushed in — and trembling with fear, he fell down before Paul and Silas.
44_16_30: And after he brought them out, he said, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
44_16_31: And they said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household."
44_16_32: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, together with all who were in his house.
44_16_33: And he took them that very hour of the night and washed their wounds — and immediately he was baptized, he and all his household.
44_16_34: And he brought them into his house and set food before them — and rejoiced greatly, having believed in God with his whole household.
44_16_35: Now when day came, the chief magistrates sent their policemen, saying, "Release those men."
44_16_36: And the jailer reported these words to Paul, saying, "The chief magistrates have sent to release you. Therefore come out now and go in peace."
44_16_37: But Paul said to them, "They have beaten us in public, without trial — men who are Romans — and have thrown us into prison. And now are they sending us away secretly? No indeed! But let them come themselves and bring us out."
44_16_38: And the policemen reported these words to the chief magistrates. And they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans —
44_16_39: and they came and appealed to them. And when they had brought them out, they kept begging them to leave the city.
44_16_40: And they went out of the prison, and entered the house of Lydia — and when they saw the brothers, they encouraged them and departed.
44_17_1: Now when they had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica — where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
44_17_2: And according to Paul's custom, he went to them — and for three Sabbaths reasoned with them from the Scriptures.
44_17_3: Explaining and giving evidence that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and saying, "This Jesus whom I am proclaiming to you is the Christ."
44_17_4: And some of them were persuaded, and joined Paul and Silas — along with a great multitude of the God-fearing Greeks, and a number of the leading women.
44_17_5: But the Jews, becoming jealous, took along some wicked men from the market place — and forming a mob, set the city in an uproar. And attacking the house of Jason, they were seeking to bring them out to the people.
44_17_6: And when they did not find them, they began dragging Jason and some brothers before the city authorities, shouting, "These men who have upset the world have come here also!
44_17_7: And Jason has welcomed them — and they all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."
44_17_8: And they stirred up the crowd and the city authorities who heard these things.
44_17_9: And when they had received a pledge from Jason and the others, they released them.
44_17_10: And the brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea — and when they arrived, they went into the synagogue of the Jews.
44_17_11: Now these were more noble-minded than those in Thessalonica, for they received the word with great eagerness — examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.
44_17_12: Therefore many of them believed — along with a number of prominent Greek women and men.
44_17_13: But when the Jews of Thessalonica found out that the word of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Berea also, they came there as well — agitating and stirring up the crowds.
44_17_14: And then immediately the brothers sent Paul out to go as far as the sea — and Silas and Timothy remained there.
44_17_15: Now those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens — and receiving a command for Silas and Timothy to come to him as soon as possible, they departed.
44_17_16: Now while Paul was waiting for them at Athens, his spirit was being provoked within him as he was observing the city full of idols.
44_17_17: So he was reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews and the God-fearing Gentiles — and in the market place every day with those who happened to be present.
44_17_18: And also some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were conversing with him. And some were saying, "What would this idle babbler wish to say?" Others, "He seems to be a proclaimer of strange deities" — because he was preaching Jesus and the resurrection.
44_17_19: And they took him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, "May we know what this new teaching is which you are proclaiming?
44_17_20: For you are bringing some strange things to our ears. Therefore we want to know what these things mean."
44_17_21: (Now all the Athenians and the strangers visiting there used to spend their time in nothing other than telling or hearing something new.)
44_17_22: So Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus, and said: "Men of Athens, I observe that you are very religious in all respects.
44_17_23: For while I was passing through and examining the objects of your worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.' Therefore what you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim to you.
44_17_24: The God who made the world and all things in it — since He is Lord of heaven and earth — does not dwell in temples made with hands.
44_17_25: Nor is He served by human hands, as though He needed anything — since He Himself gives to all life and breath and all things.
44_17_26: And He made from one man every nation of mankind to live on all the face of the earth — having determined their appointed times, and the boundaries of their habitation.
44_17_27: That they would seek God, if perhaps they might grope for Him and find Him — though He is not far from each one of us.
44_17_28: For in Him we live, and move, and exist — as even some of your own poets have said: 'For we also are His offspring.'
44_17_29: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold or silver or stone — an image formed by the art and thought of man.
44_17_30: Therefore having overlooked the times of ignorance, God is now declaring to men that all people everywhere should repent.
44_17_31: Because He has fixed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness — through a Man whom He has appointed, having furnished proof to all men by raising Him from the dead."
44_17_32: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some began to sneer — but others said, "We shall hear you again concerning this."
44_17_33: So Paul went out of their midst.
44_17_34: But some men joined him and believed — among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
44_18_1: After these things he left Athens and went to Corinth.
44_18_2: And he found a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, having recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla — because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to leave Rome. And he came to them,
44_18_3: and because he was of the same trade, he was staying with them — and they were working, for by trade they were tent-makers.
44_18_4: And he was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath — and trying to persuade Jews and Greeks.
44_18_5: But when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul began devoting himself completely to the word — solemnly testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
44_18_6: And when they resisted and blasphemed, he shook out his garments and said to them, "Your blood be upon your own heads! I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
44_18_7: And he departed from there and went to the house of a certain man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God — whose house was next to the synagogue.
44_18_8: And Crispus, the leader of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his household. And many of the Corinthians, when they heard, were believing and being baptized.
44_18_9: And the Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision: "Do not be afraid any longer — but go on speaking, and do not be silent.
44_18_10: For I am with you, and no man will attack you in order to harm you — for I have many people in this city."
44_18_11: And he settled there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
44_18_12: But while Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,
44_18_13: saying, "This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law."
44_18_14: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews: "If it were a matter of some misdemeanor or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to put up with you.
44_18_15: But if there are questions about words and names, and your own law — see to it yourselves; I am unwilling to be a judge of these matters."
44_18_16: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
44_18_17: And they all took hold of Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue, and began beating him in front of the judgment seat. But Gallio was not concerned about any of these things.
44_18_18: And Paul, having remained many days longer, took leave of the brothers, and put out to sea for Syria, and with him were Priscilla and Aquila — having had his hair cut at Cenchrea, for he was keeping a vow.
44_18_19: And they came to Ephesus, and he left them there. Now he himself entered the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
44_18_20: And when they asked him to stay for a longer time, he did not consent —
44_18_21: but taking leave of them, and saying, "I will return to you again if God wills," he set sail from Ephesus.
44_18_22: And when he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church — and went down to Antioch.
44_18_23: And having spent some time there, he departed, and passed successively through the Galatian region and Phrygia — strengthening all the disciples.
44_18_24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus — and he was mighty in the Scriptures.
44_18_25: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord — and being fervent in spirit, he was speaking and teaching accurately the things concerning Jesus, being acquainted only with the baptism of John.
44_18_26: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
44_18_27: And when he wanted to go across to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to welcome him. And when he had arrived, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace —
44_18_28: for he powerfully refuted the Jews in public, demonstrating by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
44_19_1: It happened that while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus — and found some disciples.
44_19_2: And he said to them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" And they said to him, "No, we have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit."
44_19_3: And he said, "Into what then were you baptized?" And they said, "Into John's baptism."
44_19_4: And Paul said, "John baptized with the baptism of repentance — telling the people to believe in Him who was coming after him, that is, in Jesus."
44_19_5: And when they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
44_19_6: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them — and they began speaking with tongues and prophesying.
44_19_7: And there were in all about twelve men.
44_19_8: And he entered the synagogue and continued speaking out boldly for three months — reasoning and persuading them about the kingdom of God.
44_19_9: But when some were becoming hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and took away the disciples — reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.
44_19_10: And this took place for two years — so that all who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
44_19_11: And God was performing extraordinary miracles by the hands of Paul.
44_19_12: So that handkerchiefs or aprons were even carried from his body to the sick — and the diseases left them, and the evil spirits went out.
44_19_13: But also some of the Jewish exorcists, who went from place to place, attempted to name over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus — saying, "I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches."
44_19_14: And seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
44_19_15: And the evil spirit answered and said to them, "I recognize Jesus, and I know about Paul — but who are you?"
44_19_16: And the man, in whom was the evil spirit, leaped on them and subdued all of them, and overpowered them — so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
44_19_17: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived in Ephesus. And fear fell upon them all — and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
44_19_18: Many also of those who had believed kept coming, confessing and disclosing their practices.
44_19_19: And many of those who practiced magic brought their books together and began burning them in the sight of all. And they counted up the price of them and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
44_19_20: So the word of the Lord was growing mightily and prevailing.
44_19_21: Now after these things were finished, Paul purposed in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia — saying, "After I have been there, I must also see Rome."
44_19_22: And having sent into Macedonia two of those who ministered to him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.
44_19_23: And about that time there occurred no small disturbance concerning the Way.
44_19_24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, was bringing no little business to the craftsmen.
44_19_25: These he gathered together, with the workmen of similar trades, and said: "Men, you know that our prosperity depends upon this business.
44_19_26: And you see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in almost all of Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable number of people — saying that gods made with hands are no gods at all.
44_19_27: And not only is there danger that this trade of ours fall into disrepute — but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis be regarded as worthless, and that she whom all of Asia and the world worship would even be dethroned from her magnificence."
44_19_28: And when they heard this and were filled with rage, they began crying out, saying, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
44_19_29: And the city was filled with the confusion. And they rushed with one accord into the theater — dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's traveling companions from Macedonia.
44_19_30: And when Paul wanted to go into the assembly, the disciples would not let him.
44_19_31: And also some of the Asiarchs, who were friends of his, sent to him and repeatedly urged him not to venture into the theater.
44_19_32: So then, some were shouting one thing and some another — for the assembly was in confusion, and the majority did not know for what cause they had come together.
44_19_33: And some of the crowd concluded it was Alexander, since the Jews had put him forward. And having motioned with his hand, Alexander was intending to make a defense to the assembly.
44_19_34: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, a single outcry arose from them all as they shouted for about two hours: "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
44_19_35: And after quieting the multitude, the town clerk said: "Men of Ephesus, what man is there after all who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis, and of the image which fell down from heaven?
44_19_36: Since then these are undeniable facts, you ought to keep calm and to do nothing rash.
44_19_37: For you have brought these men here who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess.
44_19_38: So then, if Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a complaint against any man, the courts are in session and proconsuls are available — let them bring charges against one another.
44_19_39: But if you want anything beyond this, it shall be settled in the lawful assembly.
44_19_40: For indeed we are in danger of being accused of a riot in connection with today's affair, since there is no real cause for it. And in this connection we shall be unable to account for this disorderly gathering."
44_19_41: And after saying this he dismissed the assembly.
44_20_1: And after the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples — and after exhorting them and taking his leave of them, he departed to go to Macedonia.
44_20_2: And when he had gone through those districts and had given them much exhortation, he came to Greece.
44_20_3: And there he spent three months. And when a plot was formed against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he decided to return through Macedonia.
44_20_4: And he was accompanied by Sopater of Berea, the son of Pyrrhus — and by Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
44_20_5: But these had gone on ahead and were waiting for us at Troas.
44_20_6: And we sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas within five days — where we spent seven days.
44_20_7: And on the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread, Paul began talking to them, intending to depart the next day — and he prolonged his message until midnight.
44_20_8: And there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered together.
44_20_9: And there was a certain young man named Eutychus sitting on the window sill, sinking into a deep sleep — and as Paul kept on talking, he was overcome by sleep and fell down from the third floor, and was picked up dead.
44_20_10: But Paul went down and fell upon him, and after embracing him said, "Do not be troubled — for his life is in him."
44_20_11: And when he had gone back up and had broken the bread and eaten, he talked with them a long while — until daybreak — and then left.
44_20_12: And they took away the boy alive — and were greatly comforted.
44_20_13: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos — intending from there to take Paul on board. For so he had arranged it, intending himself to go by land.
44_20_14: And when he met us at Assos, we took him on board and came to Mitylene.
44_20_15: And sailing from there, we arrived the following day opposite Chios — and the next day we crossed over to Samos, and the day following we came to Miletus.
44_20_16: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he would not have to spend time in Asia — for he was hurrying, if possible, to be in Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
44_20_17: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the church.
44_20_18: And when they had come to him, he said to them: "You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you the whole time —
44_20_19: serving the Lord with all humility and with tears, and with trials which came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
44_20_20: How I did not shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable — and teaching you publicly and from house to house.
44_20_21: Solemnly testifying to both Jews and Greeks of repentance toward God, and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
44_20_22: And now, behold, bound by the Spirit, I am on my way to Jerusalem — not knowing what will happen to me there.
44_20_23: Except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.
44_20_24: But I do not consider my life of any account as dear to myself — so that I may finish my course, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly of the gospel of the grace of God.
44_20_25: And now, behold, I know that all of you, among whom I went about preaching the kingdom, will see my face no more.
44_20_26: Therefore, I testify to you this day, that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
44_20_27: For I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole purpose of God.
44_20_28: Be on guard for yourselves, and for all the flock — among which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers — to shepherd the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
44_20_29: I know that after my departure savage wolves will come in among you, not sparing the flock.
44_20_30: And from among your own selves men will arise, speaking perverse things — to draw away the disciples after them.
44_20_31: Therefore be on the alert, remembering that night and day for a period of three years I did not cease to admonish each one with tears.
44_20_32: And now I commend you to God and to the word of His grace — which is able to build you up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
44_20_33: I have coveted no one's silver or gold or clothes.
44_20_34: You yourselves know that these hands ministered to my own needs, and to the men who were with me.
44_20_35: In everything I showed you that by working hard in this manner you must help the weak — and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"
44_20_36: And when he had said these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
44_20_37: And they began to weep aloud, and embraced Paul and were kissing him —
44_20_38: grieving especially over the word which he had spoken — that they would not see his face again. And they were accompanying him to the ship.
44_21_1: And it came about that when we had parted from them and had set sail, we ran a straight course to Cos — and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
44_21_2: And having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
44_21_3: And when we came in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left, we kept sailing to Syria — and landed at Tyre. For the ship was to unload its cargo there.
44_21_4: And after looking up the disciples, we stayed there seven days. And they kept telling Paul, through the Spirit, not to set foot in Jerusalem.
44_21_5: And when our days there were ended, we departed and started on our journey — while they all, with wives and children, escorted us until we were out of the city. And after kneeling down on the beach and praying, we said farewell to one another.
44_21_6: Then we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.
44_21_7: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais — and after greeting the brothers, we stayed with them for a day.
44_21_8: And on the next day we departed and came to Caesarea — and entering the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we stayed with him.
44_21_9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who were prophetesses.
44_21_10: And as we were staying there for some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
44_21_11: And coming to us, he took Paul's belt and bound his own feet and hands, and said, "This is what the Holy Spirit says: 'In this way the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt — and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
44_21_12: And when we had heard this, we as well as the local residents began begging him not to go up to Jerusalem.
44_21_13: Then Paul answered, "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
44_21_14: And since he would not be persuaded, we fell silent, remarking, "The will of the Lord be done."
44_21_15: And after these days we got ready and started on our way up to Jerusalem.
44_21_16: And some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us — taking us to Mnason of Cyprus, a disciple of long standing, with whom we were to lodge.
44_21_17: And when we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.
44_21_18: And now on the following day, Paul went in with us to James — and all the elders were present.
44_21_19: And after he had greeted them, he began to relate one by one the things which God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
44_21_20: And when they heard it they began glorifying God — and they said to him, "You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed — and they are all zealous for the Law.
44_21_21: And they have been told about you, that you are teaching all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses — telling them not to circumcise their children, nor to walk according to the customs.
44_21_22: What, then, is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.
44_21_23: Therefore do this that we tell you: we have four men who are under a vow.
44_21_24: Take them and purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses in order that they may shave their heads. And all will know that there is nothing to the things which they have been told about you — but that you yourself also walk orderly, keeping the Law.
44_21_25: But concerning the Gentiles who have believed, we wrote, having decided that they should abstain from meat sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication."
44_21_26: Then Paul took the men, and the next day, purifying himself along with them, went into the temple — giving notice of the completion of the days of purification, until the sacrifice was offered for each one of them.
44_21_27: And when the seven days were almost over, the Jews from Asia, upon seeing him in the temple, began to stir up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
44_21_28: crying out: "Men of Israel, come to our aid! This is the man who preaches to all men everywhere against our people, and the Law, and this place. And besides, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place."
44_21_29: (For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.)
44_21_30: And all the city was provoked — and the people rushed together. And taking hold of Paul, they dragged him out of the temple — and immediately the doors were shut.
44_21_31: And while they were seeking to kill him, a report came up to the commander of the Roman cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion.
44_21_32: And at once he took along some soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. And when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
44_21_33: Then the commander came up and took hold of him, and ordered him to be bound with two chains — and began asking who he was and what he had done.
44_21_34: But among the crowd some were shouting one thing and some another. And when he could not find out the facts on account of the uproar, he ordered him to be brought into the barracks.
44_21_35: And when he got to the stairs, it so happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.
44_21_36: For the multitude of the people kept following behind, crying out, "Away with him!"
44_21_37: And as Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he said to the commander, "May I say something to you?" And he said, "Do you know Greek?
44_21_38: Then you are not the Egyptian who some time ago stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Assassins out into the wilderness?"
44_21_39: But Paul said, "I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city — and I beg you, allow me to speak to the people."
44_21_40: And when he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, motioned to the people with his hand. And when there was a great hush, he spoke to them in the Hebrew dialect, saying:
44_22_1: "Brothers and fathers — hear my defense which I now offer to you."
44_22_2: And when they heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew dialect, they became even more quiet — and he said:
44_22_3: "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city — educated under Gamaliel, strictly according to the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, just as you all are today.
44_22_4: And I persecuted this Way to the death — binding and putting both men and women into prisons.
44_22_5: As also the high priest and all the Council of the elders can testify. From them I also received letters to the brothers — and I started off for Damascus in order to bring even those who were there to Jerusalem as prisoners, to be punished.
44_22_6: And it came about that as I was on my way, approaching Damascus about noontime — a very bright light suddenly flashed from heaven all around me.
44_22_7: And I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
44_22_8: And I answered, 'Who are You, Lord?' And He said to me, 'I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.'
44_22_9: And those who were with me beheld the light, to be sure, but did not understand the voice of the One who was speaking to me.
44_22_10: And I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' And the Lord said to me, 'Arise and go on into Damascus — and there you will be told of all that has been appointed for you to do.'
44_22_11: But since I could not see because of the brightness of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me — and came into Damascus.
44_22_12: And a certain Ananias, a man who was devout by the standard of the Law, and well spoken of by all the Jews who lived there,
44_22_13: came to me, and standing near said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight!' And at that very moment I looked up at him.
44_22_14: And he said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will — and to see the Righteous One, and to hear an utterance from His mouth.
44_22_15: For you will be a witness for Him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
44_22_16: And now why do you delay? Arise — and be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on His name.'
44_22_17: And it came about, when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance —
44_22_18: and I saw Him saying to me: 'Make haste, and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.'
44_22_19: And I said, 'Lord, they themselves understand that in one synagogue after another I used to imprison and beat those who believed in You.
44_22_20: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was being shed, I also was standing by, approving — and watching out for the cloaks of those who were slaying him.'
44_22_21: And He said to me, 'Go! For I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"
44_22_22: And they listened to him up to this statement, and then they raised their voices and said, "Away with such a fellow from the earth! For he should not be allowed to live!"
44_22_23: And as they were crying out and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,
44_22_24: the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, stating that he should be examined by scourging — so that he might find out the reason why they were shouting against him that way.
44_22_25: And when they stretched him out with thongs, Paul said to the centurion who was standing by, "Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and uncondemned?"
44_22_26: And when the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and told him, saying, "What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman."
44_22_27: And the commander came and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?" And he said, "Yes."
44_22_28: And the commander answered, "I acquired this citizenship with a large sum of money." And Paul said, "But I was actually born a citizen."
44_22_29: Therefore those who were about to examine him immediately let go of him. And the commander also was afraid when he found out that he was a Roman, and because he had put him in chains.
44_22_30: But on the next day, wishing to know for certain why he had been accused by the Jews, he released him — and ordered the chief priests and all the Council to assemble. And he brought Paul down and set him before them.
44_23_1: And Paul, looking intently at the Council, said, "Brothers, I have lived my life with a perfectly good conscience before God up to this day."
44_23_2: And the high priest Ananias commanded those standing beside him to strike him on the mouth.
44_23_3: Then Paul said to him, "God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall! And do you sit to try me according to the Law — and in violation of the Law order me to be struck?"
44_23_4: But the bystanders said, "Do you revile God's high priest?"
44_23_5: And Paul said, "I was not aware, brothers, that he was high priest — for it is written: 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"
44_23_6: But perceiving that one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, Paul began crying out in the Council, "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. I am on trial for the hope and resurrection of the dead!"
44_23_7: And as he said this, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and Sadducees — and the assembly was divided.
44_23_8: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor an angel, nor a spirit — but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.
44_23_9: And there arose a great uproar. And some of the scribes of the Pharisaic party stood up and began to argue heatedly, saying, "We find nothing wrong with this man. Suppose a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?"
44_23_10: And as a great dissension was developing, the commander was afraid Paul would be torn to pieces by them — and ordered the troops to go down and take him away from them by force, and bring him into the barracks.
44_23_11: But on the following night the Lord stood at his side and said, "Take courage. For as you have solemnly witnessed to My cause at Jerusalem, so you must witness also at Rome."
44_23_12: And when it was day, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves under an oath, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.
44_23_13: And there were more than forty who formed this plot.
44_23_14: And they came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, "We have bound ourselves under a solemn oath to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.
44_23_15: Now therefore, you and the Council notify the commander to bring him down to you, as though you were going to determine his case by a more thorough investigation — and we for our part are ready to slay him before he comes near the place."
44_23_16: But the son of Paul's sister heard of their ambush, and he came and entered the barracks and told Paul.
44_23_17: And Paul called one of the centurions to him and said, "Lead this young man to the commander — for he has something to report to him."
44_23_18: So he took him and led him to the commander, and said, "Paul the prisoner called me to him and asked me to lead this young man to you, since he has something to tell you."
44_23_19: And the commander took him by the hand, and stepping aside, began to inquire of him privately, "What is it that you have to report to me?"
44_23_20: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down tomorrow to the Council, as though they were going to inquire somewhat more thoroughly about him.
44_23_21: Therefore do not listen to them — for more than forty of them are lying in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse not to eat or drink until they slay him. And now they are ready and waiting for the promise from you."
44_23_22: Therefore the commander let the young man go, instructing him: "Tell no one that you have notified me of these things."
44_23_23: And he called to him two of the centurions, and said, "Get ready by the third hour of the night two hundred soldiers — and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, to proceed to Caesarea.
44_23_24: Also provide mounts to put Paul on, and bring him safely to Felix the governor."
44_23_25: And he wrote a letter having this form:
44_23_26: "Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix — greetings.
44_23_27: When this man was seized by the Jews and was about to be slain by them, I came upon them with the troops and rescued him — having learned that he was a Roman.
44_23_28: And wanting to ascertain the charge for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their Council.
44_23_29: And I found him to be accused over questions about their Law — but under no accusation deserving death or imprisonment.
44_23_30: And when I was informed that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once — also instructing his accusers to bring charges against him before you."
44_23_31: So the soldiers, in accordance with their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
44_23_32: But the next day, leaving the horsemen to go on with him, they returned to the barracks.
44_23_33: And when these had come to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.
44_23_34: And when he had read it, he asked from what province he was — and when he learned that he was from Cilicia,
44_23_35: he said, "I will give you a hearing after your accusers arrive also." And he gave orders for him to be kept in Herod's Praetorium.
44_24_1: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders, with a certain attorney named Tertullus — and they brought charges to the governor against Paul.
44_24_2: And after Paul had been summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying to the governor: "Since we have through you attained much peace, and since by your providence reforms are being carried out for this nation,
44_24_3: we acknowledge this in every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
44_24_4: But that I may not weary you any further, I beg you to grant us, by your kindness, a brief hearing.
44_24_5: For we have found this man a real pest — and a fellow who stirs up dissension among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
44_24_6: And he even tried to desecrate the temple — and then we arrested him.
44_24_8: By examining him yourself concerning all these matters, you will be able to ascertain the things of which we accuse him."
44_24_9: And the Jews also joined in the attack, asserting that these things were so.
44_24_10: And when the governor had nodded for him to speak, Paul responded: "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge to this nation, I cheerfully make my defense.
44_24_11: Since you can take note of the fact that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
44_24_12: And neither in the temple, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city itself did they find me carrying on a discussion with anyone, or causing a riot.
44_24_13: Nor can they prove to you the charges of which they now accuse me.
44_24_14: But this I admit to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, I do serve the God of our fathers — believing everything that is in accordance with the Law, and that is written in the Prophets.
44_24_15: Having a hope in God, which these men cherish themselves — that there shall certainly be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
44_24_16: In view of this, I also do my best to maintain always a blameless conscience both before God and before men.
44_24_17: Now after several years I came to bring alms to my nation, and to present offerings.
44_24_18: In which they found me occupied in the temple, having been purified — without any crowd or uproar. But there were certain Jews from Asia,
44_24_19: who ought to have been present before you, and to make accusation, should they have anything against me.
44_24_20: Or else let these men themselves tell what misdeed they found when I stood before the Council,
44_24_21: other than for this one statement which I shouted out while standing among them: 'For the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you today!'"
44_24_22: But Felix, having a more exact knowledge about the Way, put them off, saying, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case."
44_24_23: And he gave orders to the centurion for him to be kept in custody and yet have some freedom — and not to prevent any of his friends from ministering to him.
44_24_24: But some days later, Felix arrived with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess — and sent for Paul, and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
44_24_25: And as he was discussing righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix became frightened and said, "Go away for the present, and when I find time, I will summon you."
44_24_26: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given him by Paul — therefore he also used to send for him quite often, and converse with him.
44_24_27: But after two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus — and wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul imprisoned.
44_25_1: Festus therefore, having arrived in the province, three days later went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
44_25_2: And the chief priests and the leading men of the Jews brought charges against Paul — and they were urging him,
44_25_3: requesting a concession against Paul — that he might have him brought to Jerusalem. (At the same time, setting an ambush to kill him on the way.)
44_25_4: Festus then answered that Paul was being kept in custody at Caesarea — and that he himself was about to leave shortly.
44_25_5: "Therefore," he said, "let the influential men among you go down with me — and if there is anything wrong about the man, let them prosecute him."
44_25_6: And after he had spent not more than eight or ten days among them, he went down to Caesarea — and on the next day he took his seat on the tribunal, and ordered Paul to be brought.
44_25_7: And after Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him — bringing many and serious charges against him, which they could not prove.
44_25_8: And Paul said in his own defense: "I have committed no offense either against the Law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar."
44_25_9: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, answered Paul and said, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and stand trial before me on these charges?"
44_25_10: But Paul said: "I am standing before Caesar's tribunal, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also very well know.
44_25_11: If, then, I am a wrongdoer, and have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if none of those things is true of which these men accuse me — no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar."
44_25_12: Then Festus, when he had conferred with his council, answered, "You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go."
44_25_13: Now after several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, having come to pay their respects to Festus.
44_25_14: And while they were spending many days there, Festus laid Paul's case before the king, saying, "There is a certain man left as a prisoner by Felix.
44_25_15: And when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him — asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.
44_25_16: And I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to hand over any man before the accused meets his accusers face to face — and has an opportunity to make his defense against the charges.
44_25_17: Therefore, when they had assembled here, without delay I took my seat on the tribunal the next day and ordered the man to be brought.
44_25_18: And when the accusers stood up, they began bringing charges against him — not of such crimes as I was expecting.
44_25_19: But they simply had some points of disagreement with him about their own religion, and about a certain dead man, Jesus — whom Paul asserted to be alive.
44_25_20: And being at a loss how to investigate such matters, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there stand trial on these matters.
44_25_21: But when Paul appealed to be held in custody for the Emperor's decision, I ordered him to be kept in custody until I send him to Caesar."
44_25_22: And Agrippa said to Festus, "I also would like to hear the man myself." "Tomorrow," he said, "you shall hear him."
44_25_23: And so on the next day, when Agrippa came together with Bernice amid great pomp, and entered the auditorium — accompanied by the commanders and the prominent men of the city — at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.
44_25_24: And Festus said: "King Agrippa, and all you gentlemen here present with us — you behold this man about whom all the people of the Jews appealed to me, both at Jerusalem and here, loudly declaring that he ought not to live any longer.
44_25_25: But I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death. And since he himself appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
44_25_26: But I have nothing definite about him to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him before you all — and especially before you, King Agrippa — so that, after the investigation has taken place, I may have something to write.
44_25_27: For it seems absurd to me, in sending a prisoner, not to indicate also the charges against him."
44_26_1: And Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." Then Paul stretched out his hand and proceeded to make his defense:
44_26_2: "In regard to all the things of which I am accused by the Jews, I consider myself fortunate, King Agrippa, that I am about to make my defense before you today.
44_26_3: Especially because you are an expert in all customs and questions among the Jews — therefore I beg you to listen to me patiently.
44_26_4: So then, all Jews know my manner of life from my youth up — which from the beginning was spent among my own nation, and at Jerusalem.
44_26_5: Since they have known about me for a long time — if they are willing to testify — that I lived as a Pharisee according to the strictest sect of our religion.
44_26_6: And now I am standing trial for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers —
44_26_7: the promise to which our twelve tribes hope to attain — as they earnestly serve God night and day. And for this hope, O King, I am being accused by the Jews.
44_26_8: Why is it considered incredible among you people if God does raise the dead?
44_26_9: So then, I thought to myself that I had to do many things hostile to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
44_26_10: And this is just what I did in Jerusalem. Not only did I lock up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests — but also when they were being put to death, I cast my vote against them.
44_26_11: And as I punished them often in all the synagogues, I tried to force them to blaspheme. And being furiously enraged at them, I kept pursuing them even to foreign cities.
44_26_12: While thus engaged, as I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,
44_26_13: at midday, O King, I saw on the way a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining all around me and those who were journeying with me.
44_26_14: And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew dialect: 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'
44_26_15: And I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' And the Lord said, 'I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.
44_26_16: But arise, and stand on your feet. For this purpose I have appeared to you — to appoint you a minister and a witness, not only to the things which you have seen, but also to the things in which I will appear to you.
44_26_17: Delivering you from the Jewish people, and from the Gentiles — to whom I am sending you,
44_26_18: to open their eyes — so that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, in order that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and an inheritance among those who have been sanctified by faith in Me.'
44_26_19: Consequently, King Agrippa, I did not prove disobedient to the heavenly vision.
44_26_20: But kept declaring both to those of Damascus first, and also at Jerusalem, and then throughout all the region of Judea, and even to the Gentiles — that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds appropriate to repentance.
44_26_21: For this reason some Jews seized me in the temple and tried to put me to death.
44_26_22: And so, having obtained help from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great — stating nothing but what the Prophets and Moses said was going to take place.
44_26_23: That the Christ was to suffer, and that by reason of His resurrection from the dead He would be the first to proclaim light both to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles."
44_26_24: And while Paul was saying this in his defense, Festus said in a loud voice, "Paul, you are out of your mind! Your great learning is driving you mad."
44_26_25: But Paul said, "I am not out of my mind, most excellent Festus — but I utter words of sober truth.
44_26_26: For the king knows about these matters — and to him I speak with confidence, since I am persuaded that none of these things escape his notice. For this has not been done in a corner.
44_26_27: King Agrippa, do you believe the Prophets? I know that you do."
44_26_28: And Agrippa replied to Paul, "In a short time you will persuade me to become a Christian."
44_26_29: And Paul said, "I would to God, that whether in a short or long time, not only you, but also all who hear me this day, might become such as I am — except for these chains."
44_26_30: And the king arose, and the governor, and Bernice — and those who were sitting with them.
44_26_31: And when they had withdrawn, they began talking to one another, saying, "This man is not doing anything worthy of death or imprisonment."
44_26_32: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
44_27_1: And when it was decided that we should sail for Italy, they proceeded to deliver Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion of the Augustan cohort, named Julius.
44_27_2: And embarking in an Adramyttian ship, which was about to sail to the regions along the coast of Asia, we put out to sea — accompanied by Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica.
44_27_3: And the next day we put in at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul with consideration, and allowed him to go to his friends and receive care.
44_27_4: And from there we put out to sea and sailed under the shelter of Cyprus — because the winds were contrary.
44_27_5: And when we had sailed through the sea along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.
44_27_6: And there the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy — and he put us aboard it.
44_27_7: And when we had sailed slowly for a good many days, and with difficulty had arrived off Cnidus — since the wind did not permit us to go farther, we sailed under the shelter of Crete, off Salmone.
44_27_8: And with difficulty sailing past it, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens — near which was the city of Lasea.
44_27_9: And when considerable time had passed, and the voyage was now dangerous, since even the fast was already over, Paul began to admonish them,
44_27_10: and said to them, "Men, I perceive that the voyage will certainly be with damage and great loss — not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives."
44_27_11: But the centurion was more persuaded by the pilot and the captain of the ship, than by what was being said by Paul.
44_27_12: And because the harbor was not suitable for wintering, the majority reached a decision to put out to sea from there — if somehow they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete, looking northeast and southeast, and spend the winter there.
44_27_13: And when a moderate south wind came up, supposing that they had attained their purpose, they weighed anchor and began sailing along Crete, close inshore.
44_27_14: But before very long there rushed down from the land a violent wind, called Euraquilo.
44_27_15: And when the ship was caught in it, and could not face the wind, we gave way to it and let ourselves be driven along.
44_27_16: And running under the shelter of a small island called Clauda, we were scarcely able to get the ship's boat under control.
44_27_17: And after they had hoisted it up, they used supporting cables in undergirding the ship. And fearing that they might run aground on the shallows of Syrtis, they let down the sea anchor — and so let themselves be driven along.
44_27_18: And the next day as we were being violently storm-tossed, they began to jettison the cargo.
44_27_19: And on the third day they threw the ship's tackle overboard with their own hands.
44_27_20: And since neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm was assailing us — from then on all hope of our being saved was gradually abandoned.
44_27_21: And when they had gone a long time without food, then Paul stood up in their midst and said: "Men, you ought to have followed my advice, and not have set sail from Crete, and incurred this damage and loss.
44_27_22: And yet now I urge you to keep up your courage — for there shall be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
44_27_23: For this very night an angel of the God to whom I belong, and whom I serve, stood before me —
44_27_24: saying, 'Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. And behold, God has granted you all those who are sailing with you.'
44_27_25: Therefore, keep up your courage, men — for I believe God that it will turn out exactly as I have been told.
44_27_26: But we must run aground on a certain island."
44_27_27: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were being driven about in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors began to surmise that they were approaching some land.
44_27_28: And they took soundings, and found it to be twenty fathoms. And a little farther on they took another sounding, and found it to be fifteen fathoms.
44_27_29: And fearing that we might run aground somewhere on the rocks, they cast four anchors from the stern, and wished for daybreak.
44_27_30: And as the sailors were trying to escape from the ship, and had let down the ship's boat into the sea — on the pretense that they were going to lay out anchors from the bow,
44_27_31: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, "Unless these men remain in the ship, you yourselves cannot be saved."
44_27_32: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship's boat, and let it fall away.
44_27_33: And until the day was about to dawn, Paul was encouraging them all to take some food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day that you have been constantly watching and going without eating, having taken nothing.
44_27_34: Therefore I encourage you to take some food — for this is for your preservation. For not a hair from the head of any of you shall perish."
44_27_35: And having said this, he took bread and gave thanks to God in the presence of all — and he broke it and began to eat.
44_27_36: And all of them were encouraged, and they themselves also took food.
44_27_37: And all of us in the ship were two hundred and seventy-six persons.
44_27_38: And when they had eaten enough, they began to lighten the ship by throwing out the wheat into the sea.
44_27_39: And when day came, they could not recognize the land — but they did observe a certain bay with a beach, and they resolved to drive the ship onto it if they could.
44_27_40: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea while at the same time they were loosening the ropes of the rudders. And hoisting the foresail to the wind, they were heading for the beach.
44_27_41: But striking a reef where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground — and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable. But the stern began to be broken up by the force of the waves.
44_27_42: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners — so that none of them should swim away and escape.
44_27_43: But the centurion, wanting to bring Paul safely through, kept them from their intention — and commanded that those who could swim should jump overboard first and get to land.
44_27_44: And the rest should follow — some on planks, and others on various things from the ship. And thus it happened that they all were brought safely to land.
44_28_1: And when they had been brought safely through, then we found out that the island was called Malta.
44_28_2: And the natives showed us extraordinary kindness — for because of the rain that had set in, and because of the cold, they kindled a fire and received us all.
44_28_3: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened itself on his hand.
44_28_4: And when the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another, "Undoubtedly this man is a murderer — and though he has been saved from the sea, justice has not allowed him to live."
44_28_5: However he shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.
44_28_6: But they were expecting that he was about to swell up, or suddenly fall down dead. But after they had waited a long time and had seen nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and began to say that he was a god.
44_28_7: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the leading man of the island, named Publius — who welcomed us and entertained us courteously three days.
44_28_8: And it came about that the father of Publius was lying in bed, afflicted with recurrent fever and dysentery. And Paul went in to see him — and after he had prayed, he laid his hands on him and healed him.
44_28_9: And after this had happened, the rest of the people on the island who had diseases were coming to him and getting cured.
44_28_10: And they also honored us with many marks of respect — and when we were setting sail, they supplied us with all we needed.
44_28_11: And at the end of three months we set sail on an Alexandrian ship which had wintered at the island — and which had the Twin Brothers for its figurehead.
44_28_12: And after we put in at Syracuse, we stayed there for three days.
44_28_13: And from there we sailed around and arrived at Rhegium — and a day later a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
44_28_14: There we found some brothers, and were invited to stay with them for seven days — and thus we came to Rome.
44_28_15: And the brothers, when they heard about us, came from there as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Inns to meet us. And when Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.
44_28_16: And when we entered Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself, with the soldier who was guarding him.
44_28_17: And it came about that after three days he called together those who were the leading men of the Jews — and when they had come together, he began saying to them: "Brothers, though I had done nothing against our people, or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
44_28_18: And when they had examined me, they were willing to release me — because there was no ground for putting me to death.
44_28_19: But when the Jews objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar — not that I had any accusation against my nation.
44_28_20: For this reason therefore, I requested to see you and to speak with you — for I am wearing this chain for the sake of the hope of Israel."
44_28_21: And they said to him, "We have neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor have any of the brothers come here and reported or spoken anything bad about you.
44_28_22: But we desire to hear from you what your views are — for concerning this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere."
44_28_23: And when they had set a day for him, they came to him at his lodging in large numbers — and he was explaining to them by solemnly testifying about the kingdom of God, and trying to persuade them concerning Jesus, from both the Law of Moses and from the Prophets, from morning until evening.
44_28_24: And some were being persuaded by the things spoken — but others would not believe.
44_28_25: And when they did not agree with one another, they began leaving after Paul had spoken one parting word: "The Holy Spirit rightly spoke through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
44_28_26: saying: 'Go to this people and say, You will keep on hearing, but will not understand — and you will keep on seeing, but will not perceive.
44_28_27: For the heart of this people has become dull, and with their ears they scarcely hear, and they have closed their eyes — lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and return, and I should heal them.'
44_28_28: Therefore let it be known to you, that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles — they will also listen."
44_28_29: (Some manuscripts add at this point: "And when he had said these things, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.")
44_28_30: And he stayed two full years in his own rented quarters — and was welcoming all who came to him,
44_28_31: preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all openness, unhindered.
41_1_1: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
41_1_2: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way —
41_1_3: the voice of one crying in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord — make His paths straight.'"
41_1_4: John came baptizing in the wilderness, and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
41_1_5: And all the country of Judea, and all the people of Jerusalem, were going out to him — and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
41_1_6: And John was clothed with camel's hair, and a leather belt around his waist — and he ate locusts and wild honey.
41_1_7: And he was preaching: "After me comes One mightier than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
41_1_8: I baptized you with water — but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
41_1_9: And it happened in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
41_1_10: And immediately, coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens being torn open — and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.
41_1_11: And a voice came from heaven: "You are My beloved Son — in You I am well pleased."
41_1_12: And immediately the Spirit drove Him out into the wilderness.
41_1_13: And He was there in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan — and He was with the wild beasts. And the angels were ministering to Him.
41_1_14: Now after John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee — preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
41_1_15: and saying, "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand. Repent — and believe in the gospel."
41_1_16: And passing along by the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net into the sea — for they were fishermen.
41_1_17: And Jesus said to them, "Follow Me, and I will make you become fishers of men."
41_1_18: And immediately they left their nets and followed Him.
41_1_19: And going on a little farther, He saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
41_1_20: And immediately He called them. And they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants, and went after Him.
41_1_21: And they entered Capernaum. And immediately on the Sabbath He entered the synagogue and began to teach.
41_1_22: And they were astonished at His teaching — for He was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
41_1_23: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit. And he cried out,
41_1_24: saying, "What have we to do with You, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are — the Holy One of God!"
41_1_25: But Jesus rebuked him, saying, "Be silent, and come out of him!"
41_1_26: And the unclean spirit, throwing him into convulsions and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.
41_1_27: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, "What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him."
41_1_28: And immediately His fame spread everywhere throughout all the surrounding region of Galilee.
41_1_29: And immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they entered the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
41_1_30: Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying sick with a fever. And immediately they spoke to Him about her.
41_1_31: And He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. And the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
41_1_32: And at evening, when the sun set, they brought to Him all who were sick — and those who were demon-possessed.
41_1_33: And the whole city was gathered together at the door.
41_1_34: And He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons — and He would not permit the demons to speak, because they knew Him.
41_1_35: And in the morning, while it was still very dark, He arose and went out and departed to a deserted place — and there He prayed.
41_1_36: And Simon and those with him went searching for Him,
41_1_37: and they found Him, and said to Him, "Everyone is looking for You."
41_1_38: And He said to them, "Let us go on to the next towns, so that I may preach there also — for that is why I came forth."
41_1_39: And He went into all of Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and casting out demons.
41_1_40: And a leper came to Him, imploring Him, and kneeling, and saying to Him, "If You are willing, You can make me clean."
41_1_41: And Jesus, moved with compassion, stretched out His hand and touched him, and said to him, "I am willing — be clean."
41_1_42: And immediately the leprosy left him, and he was cleansed.
41_1_43: And He sternly warned him, and immediately sent him away,
41_1_44: and said to him, "See that you say nothing to anyone — but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
41_1_45: But he went out and began to proclaim it freely, and to spread the news around — so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a city, but stayed outside in deserted places. And they came to Him from every direction.
41_2_1: And again He entered Capernaum after some days — and it was heard that He was in the house.
41_2_2: And immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no longer any room — not even at the door. And He was preaching the word to them.
41_2_3: And they came to Him, bringing a paralytic, carried by four men.
41_2_4: And when they could not get near Him because of the crowd, they removed the roof where He was. And when they had broken through, they let down the pallet on which the paralytic was lying.
41_2_5: And when Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, "Son, your sins are forgiven you."
41_2_6: But some of the scribes were sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts:
41_2_7: "Why does this man speak like this? He blasphemes! Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
41_2_8: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in His spirit that they reasoned thus within themselves, said to them, "Why do you reason about these things in your hearts?
41_2_9: Which is easier — to say to the paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven you' — or to say, 'Arise, take up your pallet and walk'?
41_2_10: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — He said to the paralytic —
41_2_11: "I say to you: arise, take up your pallet, and go to your house."
41_2_12: And immediately he arose, took up the pallet, and went out before them all — so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, "We never saw anything like this!"
41_2_13: And He went out again by the sea — and all the multitude came to Him, and He was teaching them.
41_2_14: As He passed by, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and He said to him, "Follow Me." And he arose and followed Him.
41_2_15: And it happened, as He was reclining at table in his house, that many tax collectors and sinners also reclined with Jesus and His disciples — for there were many, and they followed Him.
41_2_16: And when the scribes of the Pharisees saw Him eating with the tax collectors and sinners, they said to His disciples, "Why does He eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
41_2_17: And when Jesus heard it, He said to them, "Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners — to repentance."
41_2_18: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting. And they came and said to Him, "Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast — but Your disciples do not fast?"
41_2_19: And Jesus said to them, "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
41_2_20: But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken from them — and then they will fast in those days.
41_2_21: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment — for the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear is made.
41_2_22: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins — or else the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is ruined, and the skins are ruined. But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins."
41_2_23: And it came about that He was going through the grainfields on the Sabbath — and His disciples began to make their way along, picking heads of grain.
41_2_24: And the Pharisees said to Him, "Look — why do they do what is not lawful on the Sabbath?"
41_2_25: And He said to them, "Have you never read what David did, when he was in need and was hungry, he and those with him?
41_2_26: How he entered the house of God, in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the bread of the Presence — which it is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests — and also gave it to those who were with him?"
41_2_27: And He said to them, "The Sabbath was made for man — and not man for the Sabbath.
41_2_28: So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
41_3_1: And He entered again into the synagogue. And a man was there who had a withered hand.
41_3_2: And they were watching Him closely, to see if He would heal him on the Sabbath — so that they might accuse Him.
41_3_3: And He said to the man with the withered hand, "Come forward."
41_3_4: And He said to them, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?" But they were silent.
41_3_5: And after looking around at them with anger — grieved at the hardness of their heart — He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
41_3_6: And the Pharisees went out and immediately began conspiring with the Herodians against Him, as to how they might destroy Him.
41_3_7: And Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea — and a great multitude from Galilee followed.
41_3_8: And from Judea, and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and beyond the Jordan, and from the region around Tyre and Sidon — a great multitude, hearing all that He was doing, came to Him.
41_3_9: And He told His disciples to have a small boat ready for Him because of the multitude — so that they would not crush Him.
41_3_10: For He had healed many — so that all who had afflictions pressed upon Him in order to touch Him.
41_3_11: And whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, saying, "You are the Son of God!"
41_3_12: And He sternly warned them that they should not make Him known.
41_3_13: And He went up on the mountain and called to Him those He Himself wanted — and they came to Him.
41_3_14: And He appointed twelve — that they might be with Him, and that He might send them out to preach,
41_3_15: and to have authority to cast out the demons.
41_3_16: And He appointed the twelve: Simon — to whom He gave the name Peter;
41_3_17: and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James — to whom He gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder;
41_3_18: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot;
41_3_19: and Judas Iscariot — who also betrayed Him.
41_3_20: And He came into a house, and again the multitude gathered — so that they could not even eat a meal.
41_3_21: And when His own people heard of it, they went out to seize Him — for they were saying, "He is out of His mind."
41_3_22: And the scribes who came down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the prince of demons He casts out the demons."
41_3_23: And He called them to Himself and was speaking to them in parables: "How can Satan cast out Satan?
41_3_24: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
41_3_25: And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
41_3_26: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand — but is finished.
41_3_27: But no one can enter the strong man's house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man — and then he will plunder his house.
41_3_28: Truly, I say to you — all sins will be forgiven the sons of men, and whatever blasphemies they utter.
41_3_29: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness — but is guilty of an eternal sin" —
41_3_30: because they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
41_3_31: Then His mother and His brothers came. And standing outside, they sent to Him, calling Him.
41_3_32: And a multitude was sitting around Him — and they said to Him, "Behold, Your mother and Your brothers are outside seeking You."
41_3_33: And He answered them, saying, "Who is My mother, or My brothers?"
41_3_34: And looking around on those who sat about Him, He said, "Behold, My mother and My brothers!
41_3_35: For whoever does the will of God — he is My brother, and sister, and mother."
41_4_1: And He began again to teach by the sea. And a great multitude was gathered to Him, so that He got into a boat in the sea and sat down — and the whole multitude was on the land facing the sea.
41_4_2: And He taught them many things in parables. And He said to them in His teaching:
41_4_3: "Listen! Behold, the sower went out to sow.
41_4_4: And it came about, as he was sowing, that some seed fell beside the road — and the birds came and devoured it.
41_4_5: And other seed fell on the rocky ground where it did not have much soil — and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
41_4_6: And when the sun came up, it was scorched. And because it had no root, it withered away.
41_4_7: And other seed fell among the thorns — and the thorns came up and choked it, and it yielded no crop.
41_4_8: And other seed fell into the good soil — and as it grew up and increased, it yielded a crop: thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold."
41_4_9: And He was saying, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear."
41_4_10: And when He was alone, those around Him with the twelve began asking Him about the parables.
41_4_11: And He was saying to them, "To you has been granted the mystery of the kingdom of God — but to those outside, everything comes in parables.
41_4_12: So that 'while seeing they may see, and not perceive — and while hearing they may hear, and not understand. Otherwise they might return and be forgiven.'"
41_4_13: And He said to them, "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
41_4_15: And these are the ones beside the road, where the word is sown — and when they hear, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
41_4_16: And in a similar way these are the ones on whom seed was sown on the rocky places — who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy.
41_4_17: And they have no firm root in themselves, but are only temporary — then when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they fall away.
41_4_18: And others are the ones on whom seed was sown among the thorns — these are the ones who have heard the word,
41_4_19: and the worries of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things enter in — and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
41_4_20: And those on whom seed was sown on the good ground — these are the ones who hear the word and accept it, and bear fruit: thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold."
41_4_21: And He was saying to them, "A lamp is not brought to be put under a basket, or under a bed, is it? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?
