41_4_22: For nothing is hidden, except to be revealed — nor has anything been secret, but that it should come to light.
41_4_23: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."
41_4_24: And He was saying to them, "Take care what you listen to. By your standard of measure it will be measured to you — and more will be added to you.
41_4_25: For whoever has, to him more shall be given — and whoever does not have, even what he has shall be taken away from him."
41_4_26: And He was saying, "The kingdom of God is like a man who casts seed upon the soil —
41_4_27: and he sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts up and grows — how, he himself does not know.
41_4_28: The soil produces crops by itself — first the blade, then the head, then the mature grain in the head.
41_4_29: But when the crop permits, he immediately puts in the sickle — because the harvest has come."
41_4_30: And He said, "How shall we picture the kingdom of God? Or with what parable shall we present it?
41_4_31: It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown upon the soil, though it is smaller than all the seeds that are upon the soil —
41_4_32: yet when it is sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants — and forms large branches, with the result that the birds of the air can nest under its shade."
41_4_33: And with many such parables He was speaking the word to them — as they were able to hear it.
41_4_34: And He did not speak to them without a parable — but He was explaining everything privately to His own disciples.
41_4_35: And on that day, when evening had come, He said to them, "Let us go over to the other side."
41_4_36: And leaving the multitude, they took Him along with them in the boat just as He was. And other boats were with Him.
41_4_37: And there arose a fierce gale of wind — and the waves were breaking over the boat, so much that the boat was already filling up.
41_4_38: And He Himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. And they woke Him up, and said to Him, "Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?"
41_4_39: And being aroused, He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Hush — be still." And the wind died down, and it became perfectly calm.
41_4_40: And He said to them, "Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?"
41_4_41: And they became very much afraid, and were saying to one another, "Who then is this — that even the wind and the sea obey Him?"
41_5_1: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
41_5_2: And when He had come out of the boat, immediately a man from the tombs with an unclean spirit met Him —
41_5_3: and he had his dwelling among the tombs. And no one was able to bind him anymore, even with a chain.
41_5_4: Because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the shackles broken in pieces — and no one was strong enough to subdue him.
41_5_5: And constantly, night and day, among the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out and gashing himself with stones.
41_5_6: And seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran up and bowed down before Him.
41_5_7: And crying out with a loud voice, he said, "What have I to do with You, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore You by God — do not torment me!"
41_5_8: For He had been saying to him, "Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!"
41_5_9: And He was asking him, "What is your name?" And he said to Him, "My name is Legion — for we are many."
41_5_10: And he began to implore Him earnestly not to send them out of the country.
41_5_11: Now there was a big herd of swine feeding there on the mountain.
41_5_12: And the demons implored Him, saying, "Send us into the swine, so that we may enter them."
41_5_13: And He gave them permission. And coming out, the unclean spirits entered the swine — and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand of them. And they were drowned in the sea.
41_5_14: And their herdsmen ran away and reported it in the city and in the country. And the people came to see what it was that had happened.
41_5_15: And they came to Jesus and observed the man who had been demon-possessed sitting down — clothed and in his right mind — the very man who had the legion. And they became frightened.
41_5_16: And those who had seen it described to them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man — and the story of the swine.
41_5_17: And they began to implore Him to depart from their region.
41_5_18: And as He was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was imploring Him that he might accompany Him.
41_5_19: And He did not let him — but He said to him, "Go home to your people — and report to them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how He had mercy on you."
41_5_20: And he went away and began to proclaim in Decapolis what great things Jesus had done for him — and everyone was amazed.
41_5_21: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a great multitude gathered around Him. And He was by the sea.
41_5_22: And one of the synagogue officials named Jairus came up, and on seeing Him, fell at His feet,
41_5_23: and implored Him earnestly, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay Your hands on her, that she may be made well and live."
41_5_24: And He went off with him. And a great multitude was following Him and pressing in on Him.
41_5_25: And a woman who had had a hemorrhage for twelve years,
41_5_26: and had endured much at the hands of many physicians, and had spent all that she had and was not helped at all, but rather had grown worse —
41_5_27: after hearing about Jesus, came up in the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak.
41_5_28: For she thought, "If I just touch His garments, I shall get well."
41_5_29: And immediately the flow of her blood was dried up. And she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
41_5_30: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in Himself that the power proceeding from Him had gone forth, turned around in the crowd and was saying, "Who touched My garments?"
41_5_31: And His disciples said to Him, "You see the multitude pressing in on You — and You say, 'Who touched Me?'"
41_5_32: And He looked around to see the woman who had done this.
41_5_33: But the woman, fearing and trembling — knowing what had happened to her — came and fell down before Him, and told Him the whole truth.
41_5_34: And He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace — and be healed of your affliction."
41_5_35: While He was still speaking, they came from the house of the synagogue official, saying, "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher anymore?"
41_5_36: But Jesus, overhearing what was being spoken, said to the synagogue official, "Do not be afraid — only believe."
41_5_37: And He allowed no one to accompany Him, except Peter and James, and John the brother of James.
41_5_38: And they came to the house of the synagogue official — and He beheld a commotion, and people weeping and wailing loudly.
41_5_39: And entering in, He said to them, "Why make a commotion and weep? The child has not died — but is asleep."
41_5_40: And they began laughing at Him. But putting them all out, He took the child's father and mother and His own companions, and entered the room where the child was.
41_5_41: And taking the child by the hand, He said to her, "Talitha kum!" — which translated means, "Little girl, I say to you, arise!"
41_5_42: And immediately the girl arose and began to walk — for she was twelve years old. And immediately they were completely astounded.
41_5_43: And He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this — and He said that something should be given her to eat.
41_6_1: And He went out from there, and came into His hometown — and His disciples followed Him.
41_6_2: And when the Sabbath had come, He began to teach in the synagogue. And the many listeners were astonished, saying, "Where did this man get these things? And what is this wisdom given to Him — and such miracles as these performed by His hands?
41_6_3: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary — and brother of James, and Joses, and Judas, and Simon? Are not His sisters here with us?" And they took offense at Him.
41_6_4: And Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor — except in his hometown, and among his own relatives, and in his own household."
41_6_5: And He could do no miracle there — except that He laid His hands upon a few sick people, and healed them.
41_6_6: And He wondered at their unbelief. And He was going around the villages teaching.
41_6_7: And He summoned the twelve, and began to send them out in pairs — and He was giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
41_6_8: And He instructed them that they should take nothing for their journey except a mere staff — no bread, no bag, no money in their belt,
41_6_9: but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.
41_6_10: And He was saying to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave town.
41_6_11: And any place that does not receive you, or listen to you — as you go out from there, shake the dust off the soles of your feet as a testimony against them."
41_6_12: And they went out and preached that men should repent.
41_6_13: And they were casting out many demons, and were anointing with oil many sick people and healing them.
41_6_14: And King Herod heard of it — for His name had become well known. And people were saying, "John the Baptist has risen from the dead — and that is why these miraculous powers are at work in Him."
41_6_15: But others were saying, "He is Elijah." And others were saying, "He is a prophet — like one of the prophets of old."
41_6_16: But when Herod heard of it, he kept saying, "John, whom I beheaded, has risen!"
41_6_17: For Herod himself had sent and had John arrested, and bound in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip — because he had married her.
41_6_18: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
41_6_19: And Herodias had a grudge against him, and wanted to put him to death — and yet she could not;
41_6_20: for Herod was afraid of John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man — and he kept him safe. And when he heard him, he was very perplexed — but used to enjoy listening to him.
41_6_21: And a strategic day came when Herod, on his birthday, gave a banquet for his lords and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
41_6_22: And when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and his dinner guests. And the king said to the girl, "Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you."
41_6_23: And he vowed to her, "Whatever you ask of me, I will give it to you — up to half of my kingdom!"
41_6_24: And she went out and said to her mother, "What shall I ask for?" And she said, "The head of John the Baptist."
41_6_25: And immediately she came in a hurry to the king, and asked, saying, "I want you to give me right away the head of John the Baptist on a platter."
41_6_26: And although the king was very sorry, yet because of his oaths and his dinner guests, he was unwilling to refuse her.
41_6_27: And immediately the king sent an executioner — and commanded him to bring back his head. And he went and beheaded him in the prison,
41_6_28: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the girl — and the girl gave it to her mother.
41_6_29: And when his disciples heard about this, they came and took away his body — and laid it in a tomb.
41_6_30: And the apostles gathered together with Jesus — and they reported to Him all that they had done and taught.
41_6_31: And He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place — and rest a while." For there were many people coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
41_6_32: And they went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
41_6_33: And the people saw them going, and many recognized them — and they ran there together on foot from all the cities, and got there ahead of them.
41_6_34: And when He went ashore, He saw a great multitude — and He felt compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
41_6_35: And when it was already quite late, His disciples came up to Him, saying, "This place is deserted, and it is already quite late.
41_6_36: Send them away — so that they may go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
41_6_37: But He answered them, "You give them something to eat!" And they said to Him, "Shall we go and spend two hundred denarii on bread and give them something to eat?"
41_6_38: And He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go look!" And when they found out, they said, "Five — and two fish."
41_6_39: And He commanded them all to recline by groups on the green grass.
41_6_40: And they reclined in companies of hundreds and of fifties.
41_6_41: And He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, He blessed and broke the loaves, and kept giving them to the disciples to set before them. And He divided up the two fish among them all.
41_6_42: And they all ate and were satisfied.
41_6_43: And they picked up twelve full baskets of the broken pieces — and also of the fish.
41_6_44: And those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
41_6_45: And immediately He made His disciples get into the boat and go ahead of Him to the other side to Bethsaida — while He Himself was sending the multitude away.
41_6_46: And after bidding them farewell, He left for the mountain to pray.
41_6_47: And when it was evening, the boat was in the middle of the sea — and He was alone on the land.
41_6_48: And seeing them straining at the oars (for the wind was against them), at about the fourth watch of the night He came to them, walking on the sea — and He intended to pass by them.
41_6_49: But when they saw Him walking on the sea, they supposed that it was a ghost — and they cried out.
41_6_50: For they all saw Him and were frightened. But immediately He spoke with them and said to them, "Take courage — it is I. Do not be afraid."
41_6_51: And He got into the boat with them — and the wind stopped. And they were utterly astonished within themselves.
41_6_52: For they had not gained any insight from the incident of the loaves — but their heart was hardened.
41_6_53: And when they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
41_6_54: And when they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized Him,
41_6_55: and ran about that whole country, and began to carry about on their pallets those who were sick — to the place they heard He was.
41_6_56: And wherever He entered villages, or cities, or countryside, they were laying the sick in the market places — and imploring Him that they might just touch the fringe of His cloak. And as many as touched it were being healed.
41_7_1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, who had come from Jerusalem, gathered around Him.
41_7_2: And they had seen that some of His disciples were eating their bread with impure hands — that is, unwashed.
41_7_3: For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they carefully wash their hands — observing the traditions of the elders.
41_7_4: And when they come from the market place, they do not eat unless they cleanse themselves. And there are many other things which they have received in order to observe — such as the washing of cups and pitchers and copper pots.
41_7_5: And the Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, "Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders — but eat their bread with impure hands?"
41_7_6: And He said to them, "Rightly did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites — as it is written: 'This people honors Me with their lips — but their heart is far away from Me.
41_7_7: And in vain do they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the precepts of men.'
41_7_8: Neglecting the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men."
41_7_9: And He was also saying to them, "You nicely set aside the commandment of God in order to keep your tradition.
41_7_10: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.'
41_7_11: But you say, 'If a man says to his father or his mother, "Whatever I have that would help you is Corban"' — that is to say, given to God —
41_7_12: you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or his mother.
41_7_13: Thus you invalidate the word of God by your tradition which you have handed down — and you do many things such as that."
41_7_14: And after He called the multitude to Him again, He began saying to them, "Listen to Me, all of you — and understand.
41_7_15: There is nothing outside the man which going into him can defile him — but the things which proceed out of the man are what defile the man.
41_7_16: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."
41_7_17: And when leaving the multitude, He had entered the house, His disciples questioned Him about the parable.
41_7_18: And He said to them, "Are you so lacking in understanding also? Do you not see that whatever goes into the man from outside cannot defile him —
41_7_19: because it does not go into his heart, but into his stomach, and is eliminated?" (Thus He declared all foods clean.)
41_7_20: And He was saying, "That which proceeds out of the man — that is what defiles the man.
41_7_21: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed the evil thoughts — fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries,
41_7_22: deeds of coveting and wickedness, deceit, sensuality, envy, slander, pride, foolishness.
41_7_23: All these evil things proceed from within — and defile the man."
41_7_24: And from there He arose and went away to the region of Tyre. And when He had entered a house, He wanted no one to know of it — yet He could not escape notice.
41_7_25: But immediately, after hearing of Him, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit came and fell at His feet.
41_7_26: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by nationality. And she kept asking Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
41_7_27: And He was saying to her, "Let the children first be satisfied — for it is not good to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs."
41_7_28: But she answered and said to Him, "Yes, Lord — but even the little dogs under the table feed on the children's crumbs."
41_7_29: And He said to her, "Because of this answer, go your way — the demon has gone out of your daughter."
41_7_30: And going back to her home, she found the child lying on the bed — the demon having gone out.
41_7_31: And again, He went out from the region of Tyre, and came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, within the region of Decapolis.
41_7_32: And they brought to Him one who was deaf and spoke with difficulty — and they implored Him to lay His hand upon him.
41_7_33: And He took him aside from the multitude, by himself, and put His fingers into his ears. And after spitting, He touched his tongue with the saliva.
41_7_34: And looking up to heaven with a deep sigh, He said to him, "Ephphatha!" — that is, "Be opened!"
41_7_35: And his ears were opened — and the impediment of his tongue was removed, and he began speaking plainly.
41_7_36: And He gave them orders not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they continued to proclaim it.
41_7_37: And they were utterly astonished, saying, "He has done all things well — He makes even the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak."
41_8_1: In those days, when there was again a great multitude and they had nothing to eat, He called His disciples to Him and said to them,
41_8_2: "I feel compassion for the multitude, because they have remained with Me now three days — and have nothing to eat.
41_8_3: And if I send them away hungry to their home, they will faint on the way — and some of them have come from a great distance."
41_8_4: And His disciples answered Him, "Where will anyone be able to find enough bread here in this deserted place to satisfy these people?"
41_8_5: And He was asking them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven."
41_8_6: And He directed the multitude to recline on the ground. And taking the seven loaves and giving thanks, He broke them and started giving them to His disciples to serve to them — and they served them to the multitude.
41_8_7: And they also had a few small fish — and after He had blessed them, He ordered these to be served as well.
41_8_8: And they ate and were satisfied — and they picked up seven large baskets full of what was left over of the broken pieces.
41_8_9: And about four thousand were there. And He sent them away.
41_8_10: And immediately He entered the boat with His disciples, and came to the district of Dalmanutha.
41_8_11: And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven — to test Him.
41_8_12: And sighing deeply in His spirit, He said, "Why does this generation seek for a sign? Truly I say to you — no sign shall be given to this generation."
41_8_13: And leaving them, He again embarked and went away to the other side.
41_8_14: And they had forgotten to take bread — and did not have more than one loaf in the boat with them.
41_8_15: And He was giving orders to them, saying, "Watch out! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and the leaven of Herod."
41_8_16: And they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread.
41_8_17: And Jesus, aware of this, said to them, "Why do you discuss the fact that you have no bread? Do you not yet see or understand? Do you have a hardened heart?
41_8_18: Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
41_8_19: when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand — how many baskets full of broken pieces you picked up?" They said to Him, "Twelve."
41_8_20: "And when I broke the seven for the four thousand — how many large baskets full of broken pieces did you pick up?" And they said to Him, "Seven."
41_8_21: And He was saying to them, "Do you not yet understand?"
41_8_22: And they came to Bethsaida. And they brought a blind man to Jesus, and entreated Him to touch him.
41_8_23: And taking the blind man by the hand, He brought him out of the village. And after spitting on his eyes and laying His hands upon him, He asked him, "Do you see anything?"
41_8_24: And he looked up and said, "I see men — for I see them like trees, walking about."
41_8_25: Then again He laid His hands upon his eyes — and he looked intently and was restored, and began to see everything clearly.
41_8_26: And He sent him to his home, saying, "Do not even enter the village."
41_8_27: And Jesus went out, along with His disciples, to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. And on the way He questioned His disciples, saying to them, "Who do people say that I am?"
41_8_28: And they told Him, saying, "John the Baptist — and others say Elijah; but others, one of the prophets."
41_8_29: And He continued by questioning them, "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered and said to Him, "You are the Christ."
41_8_30: And He warned them to tell no one about Him.
41_8_31: And He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes — and be killed, and after three days rise again.
41_8_32: And He was stating the matter plainly. And Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.
41_8_33: But turning around and seeing His disciples, He rebuked Peter and said, "Get behind Me, Satan! For you are not setting your mind on God's interests, but man's."
41_8_34: And He summoned the multitude with His disciples, and said to them, "If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me.
41_8_35: For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it — but whoever loses his life for My sake and the gospel's shall save it.
41_8_36: For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world, and forfeit his soul?
41_8_37: For what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
41_8_38: For whoever is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation — the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels."
41_9_1: And He was saying to them, "Truly I say to you — there are some of those who are standing here who shall not taste of death, until they see the kingdom of God come with power."
41_9_2: And six days later, Jesus took with Him Peter and James and John, and brought them up to a high mountain by themselves. And He was transfigured before them.
41_9_3: And His garments became radiant — exceedingly white, as no launderer on earth can whiten them.
41_9_4: And Elijah appeared to them along with Moses — and they were talking with Jesus.
41_9_5: And Peter said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good that we are here. Let us make three tabernacles — one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
41_9_6: For he did not know what to answer — for they became terrified.
41_9_7: And a cloud formed, overshadowing them — and a voice came out of the cloud, "This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!"
41_9_8: And all at once they looked around and saw no one with them anymore — except Jesus alone.
41_9_9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, He gave them orders not to relate to anyone what they had seen — until the Son of Man should rise from the dead.
41_9_10: And they seized upon that statement, discussing with one another what rising from the dead might mean.
41_9_11: And they asked Him, saying, "Why is it that the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
41_9_12: And He said to them, "Elijah does first come and restore all things. And yet how is it written of the Son of Man, that He should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
41_9_13: But I say to you that Elijah has indeed come — and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written of him."
41_9_14: And when they came back to the disciples, they saw a great multitude around them — and some scribes arguing with them.
41_9_15: And immediately, when the entire crowd saw Him, they were amazed and began running up to greet Him.
41_9_16: And He asked them, "What are you discussing with them?"
41_9_17: And one of the crowd answered Him, "Teacher, I brought You my son, possessed with a spirit which makes him mute.
41_9_18: And whenever it seizes him, it dashes him to the ground — and he foams at the mouth, and grinds his teeth, and stiffens out. And I told Your disciples to cast it out — and they could not do it."
41_9_19: And He answered them and said, "O unbelieving generation! How long shall I be with you? How long shall I put up with you? Bring him to Me!"
41_9_20: And they brought the boy to Him. And when the spirit saw Him, immediately it threw him into a convulsion — and falling to the ground, he began rolling about, and foaming at the mouth.
41_9_21: And He asked his father, "How long has this been happening to him?" And he said, "From childhood.
41_9_22: And it has often thrown him both into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if You can do anything — take pity on us and help us!"
41_9_23: And Jesus said to him, "'If You can!' All things are possible to him who believes."
41_9_24: Immediately the boy's father cried out and was saying, "I do believe — help my unbelief!"
41_9_25: And when Jesus saw that a crowd was rapidly gathering, He rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "You deaf and dumb spirit — I command you, come out of him! And do not enter him again!"
41_9_26: And after crying out and throwing him into terrible convulsions, it came out — and the boy became so much like a corpse, that most of them said, "He is dead!"
41_9_27: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him — and he got up.
41_9_28: And when He had come into the house, His disciples began questioning Him privately, "Why could we not cast it out?"
41_9_29: And He said to them, "This kind cannot come out by anything but prayer."
41_9_30: And from there they went out and began to go through Galilee — and He was unwilling for anyone to know about it.
41_9_31: For He was teaching His disciples, and telling them, "The Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill Him. And when He has been killed, He will rise three days later."
41_9_32: But they did not understand this statement, and they were afraid to ask Him.
41_9_33: And they came to Capernaum. And when He was in the house, He began to question them, "What were you discussing on the way?"
41_9_34: But they kept silent — for on the way they had discussed with one another which one of them was the greatest.
41_9_35: And sitting down, He called the twelve and said to them, "If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all."
41_9_36: And taking a child, He set him before them. And taking him in His arms, He said to them,
41_9_37: "Whoever receives one such child in My name receives Me. And whoever receives Me, does not receive Me, but Him who sent Me."
41_9_38: John said to Him, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name — and we tried to prevent him, because he was not following us."
41_9_39: But Jesus said, "Do not hinder him — for there is no one who shall perform a miracle in My name, and be able soon afterward to speak evil of Me.
41_9_40: For he who is not against us is for us.
41_9_41: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because of your name as followers of Christ — truly I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.
41_9_42: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe to stumble — it would be better for him if, with a heavy millstone hung around his neck, he had been cast into the sea.
41_9_43: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off! It is better for you to enter life crippled, than having your two hands, to go into hell — into the unquenchable fire.
41_9_44: (Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.)
41_9_45: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off! It is better for you to enter life lame, than having your two feet, to be cast into hell.
41_9_46: (Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.)
41_9_47: And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out! It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes, to be cast into hell.
41_9_48: Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.
41_9_49: For everyone will be salted with fire.
41_9_50: Salt is good. But if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you make it salty again? Have salt in yourselves — and be at peace with one another."
41_10_1: And rising up, He went from there to the region of Judea, and beyond the Jordan. And crowds gathered around Him again — and according to His custom, He once more began to teach them.
41_10_2: And some Pharisees came up to Him, testing Him — and began to question Him whether it was lawful for a man to divorce a wife.
41_10_3: And He answered and said to them, "What did Moses command you?"
41_10_4: And they said, "Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and to send her away."
41_10_5: But Jesus said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment.
41_10_6: But from the beginning of creation, God made them male and female.
41_10_7: For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother,
41_10_8: and the two shall become one flesh — so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
41_10_9: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate."
41_10_10: And in the house the disciples began questioning Him about this again.
41_10_11: And He said to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
41_10_12: And if she herself divorces her husband and marries another man, she is committing adultery."
41_10_13: And they were bringing children to Him so that He might touch them — but the disciples rebuked them.
41_10_14: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and said to them, "Permit the children to come to Me — do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
41_10_15: Truly I say to you — whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child shall not enter it at all."
41_10_16: And He took them in His arms and began blessing them, laying His hands upon them.
41_10_17: And as He was setting out on a journey, a man ran up to Him and knelt before Him, and began asking Him, "Good Teacher — what shall I do to inherit eternal life?"
41_10_18: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except God alone.
41_10_19: You know the commandments — 'Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness. Do not defraud. Honor your father and mother.'"
41_10_20: And he said to Him, "Teacher, I have kept all these things from my youth up."
41_10_21: And looking at him, Jesus felt a love for him, and said to him, "One thing you lack — go and sell all you possess, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven. And come, follow Me!"
41_10_22: But at these words his face fell, and he went away grieved — for he was one who owned much property.
41_10_23: And Jesus, looking around, said to His disciples, "How hard it will be for those who are wealthy to enter the kingdom of God!"
41_10_24: And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus answered again and said to them, "Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
41_10_25: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
41_10_26: And they were even more astonished, and said to Him, "Then who can be saved?"
41_10_27: Looking upon them, Jesus said, "With men it is impossible — but not with God. For all things are possible with God."
41_10_28: Peter began to say to Him, "Behold, we have left everything and followed You."
41_10_29: Jesus said, "Truly I say to you — there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or mother, or father, or children, or farms, for My sake and for the gospel's sake,
41_10_30: but that he shall receive a hundred times as much now in the present age — houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and farms, along with persecutions — and in the age to come, eternal life.
41_10_31: But many who are first will be last, and the last, first."
41_10_32: And they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem — and Jesus was walking on ahead of them. And they were amazed. And those who followed were fearful. And again He took the twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him,
41_10_33: saying, "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem — and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. And they will condemn Him to death, and will deliver Him to the Gentiles.
41_10_34: And they will mock Him, and spit upon Him, and scourge Him, and kill Him — and three days later He will rise again."
41_10_35: And James and John, the two sons of Zebedee, came up to Him, saying to Him, "Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask of You."
41_10_36: And He said to them, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
41_10_37: And they said to Him, "Grant that we may sit in Your glory — one on Your right, and one on Your left."
41_10_38: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking for. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink — or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
41_10_39: And they said to Him, "We are able." And Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you shall drink — and you shall be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.
41_10_40: But to sit on My right or on My left — this is not Mine to give. But it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
41_10_41: And hearing this, the ten began to feel indignant with James and John.
41_10_42: And calling them to Himself, Jesus said to them, "You know that those who are recognized as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them. And their great men exercise authority over them.
41_10_43: But it is not so among you. But whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant.
41_10_44: And whoever wishes to be first among you shall be slave of all.
41_10_45: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve — and to give His life a ransom for many."
41_10_46: And they came to Jericho. And as He was leaving Jericho with His disciples and a great multitude, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting by the road.
41_10_47: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, "Jesus, Son of David — have mercy on me!"
41_10_48: And many were sternly telling him to be quiet. But he kept crying out all the more, "Son of David — have mercy on me!"
41_10_49: And Jesus stopped and said, "Call him here." And they called the blind man, saying to him, "Take courage — arise! He is calling for you."
41_10_50: And casting aside his cloak, he jumped up and came to Jesus.
41_10_51: And answering him, Jesus said, "What do you want Me to do for you?" And the blind man said to Him, "Rabboni — I want to regain my sight!"
41_10_52: And Jesus said to him, "Go your way. Your faith has made you well." And immediately he regained his sight, and began following Him on the road.
41_11_1: And as they approached Jerusalem, at Bethphage and Bethany, near the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples,
41_11_2: and said to them, "Go into the village opposite you — and immediately as you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no one yet has ever sat. Untie it, and bring it here.
41_11_3: And if anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?' — say, 'The Lord has need of it.' And immediately he will send it back here."
41_11_4: And they went away and found a colt tied at the door, outside in the street — and they untied it.
41_11_5: And some of the bystanders were saying to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
41_11_6: And they spoke to them just as Jesus had told them. And they gave them permission.
41_11_7: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and put their garments on it — and He sat upon it.
41_11_8: And many spread their garments in the road, and others spread leafy branches which they had cut from the fields.
41_11_9: And those who went before, and those who followed after, were crying out, "Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!
41_11_10: Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!"
41_11_11: And He entered Jerusalem and came into the temple. And after looking around at everything, He departed for Bethany with the twelve — for it was already late.
41_11_12: And on the next day, when they had departed from Bethany, He became hungry.
41_11_13: And seeing at a distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if perhaps He would find anything on it. And when He came to it, He found nothing but leaves — for it was not the season for figs.
41_11_14: And He answered and said to it, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again!" And His disciples were listening.
41_11_15: And they came to Jerusalem. And He entered the temple and began to drive out those who were buying and selling in the temple — and He overturned the tables of the money changers, and the seats of those who were selling doves.
41_11_16: And He would not permit anyone to carry merchandise through the temple.
41_11_17: And He began to teach and say to them, "Is it not written, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations'? But you have made it a robbers' den."
41_11_18: And the chief priests and the scribes heard this, and began seeking how to destroy Him — for they were afraid of Him, because all the multitude was astonished at His teaching.
41_11_19: And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
41_11_20: And as they were passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots up.
41_11_21: And being reminded, Peter said to Him, "Rabbi, behold — the fig tree which You cursed has withered."
41_11_22: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Have faith in God.
41_11_23: Truly I say to you — whoever says to this mountain, 'Be taken up and cast into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says is going to happen, it shall be granted him.
41_11_24: Therefore I say to you — all things for which you pray and ask, believe that you have received them, and they shall be granted you.
41_11_25: And whenever you stand praying, forgive — if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your transgressions.
41_11_26: (But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your transgressions.)"
41_11_27: And they came again to Jerusalem. And as He was walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to Him,
41_11_28: and began saying to Him, "By what authority are You doing these things — or who gave You this authority to do these things?"
41_11_29: And Jesus said to them, "I will ask you one question — and you answer Me, and then I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
41_11_30: Was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men? Answer Me."
41_11_31: And they began reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
41_11_32: But shall we say, 'From men'?" — they were afraid of the multitude, for all considered John to have been a real prophet.
41_11_33: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know." And Jesus said to them, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
41_12_1: And He began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, and put a wall around it, and dug a vat under the wine press, and built a tower — and rented it out to vine-growers and went on a journey.
41_12_2: And at the harvest time he sent a slave to the vine-growers, in order to receive some of the produce of the vineyard from them.
41_12_3: And they took him and beat him — and sent him away empty-handed.
41_12_4: And again he sent them another slave — and they wounded him in the head and treated him shamefully.
41_12_5: And he sent another, and that one they killed. And so with many others — beating some, and killing others.
41_12_6: He had one more, a beloved son. He sent him last of all to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
41_12_7: But those vine-growers said to one another, 'This is the heir. Come — let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours!'
41_12_8: And they took him, and killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
41_12_9: What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the vine-growers — and will give the vineyard to others.
41_12_10: Have you not even read this Scripture: 'The stone which the builders rejected — this became the chief corner stone.
41_12_11: This came about from the Lord — and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
41_12_12: And they were seeking to seize Him. And yet they feared the multitude — for they understood that He spoke the parable against them. And so they left Him and went away.
41_12_13: And they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to Him, in order to trap Him in a statement.
41_12_14: And they came and said to Him, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful, and defer to no one. For You are not partial to any — but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful to pay a poll-tax to Caesar, or not?
41_12_15: Shall we pay, or shall we not pay?" But He, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, "Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to look at."
41_12_16: And they brought one. And He said to them, "Whose likeness and inscription is this?" And they said to Him, "Caesar's."
41_12_17: And Jesus said to them, "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's — and to God the things that are God's." And they were amazed at Him.
41_12_18: And some Sadducees (who say that there is no resurrection) came to Him — and began questioning Him, saying,
41_12_19: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies, and leaves behind a wife and leaves no child, his brother should marry the wife — and raise up offspring to his brother.
41_12_20: There were seven brothers. And the first took a wife — and died, leaving no offspring.
41_12_21: And the second one took her, and died, leaving behind no offspring — and the third likewise.
41_12_22: And so all seven left no offspring. Last of all the woman also died.
41_12_23: In the resurrection, when they rise again, which one's wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife."
41_12_24: Jesus said to them, "Is this not the reason you are mistaken — that you do not understand the Scriptures, or the power of God?
41_12_25: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage — but are like angels in heaven.
41_12_26: But regarding the fact that the dead rise again — have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the burning bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?
41_12_27: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are greatly mistaken."
41_12_28: And one of the scribes came and heard them arguing, and recognized that He had answered them well — and asked Him, "Which commandment is the foremost of all?"
41_12_29: Jesus answered, "The foremost is, 'Hear, O Israel — the Lord our God is one Lord.
41_12_30: And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.'
41_12_31: The second is this — 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."
41_12_32: And the scribe said to Him, "Right, Teacher! You have truly stated that He is One — and there is no one else besides Him.
41_12_33: And to love Him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the strength — and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is much more than all burnt offerings and sacrifices."
41_12_34: And when Jesus saw that he had answered intelligently, He said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And after that, no one would venture to ask Him any more questions.
41_12_35: And Jesus, while teaching in the temple, began to say, "How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
41_12_36: David himself said in the Holy Spirit — 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand, until I put Your enemies beneath Your feet."'
41_12_37: David himself calls Him 'Lord.' And so in what sense is He his son?" And the great crowd enjoyed listening to Him.
41_12_38: And in His teaching He was saying: "Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and like respectful greetings in the market places,
41_12_39: and chief seats in the synagogues, and places of honor at banquets —
41_12_40: who devour widows' houses, and for appearance's sake offer long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation."
41_12_41: And He sat down opposite the treasury, and began observing how the multitude were putting money into the treasury. And many rich people were putting in large sums.
41_12_42: And a poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which amount to a cent.
41_12_43: And calling His disciples to Him, He said to them, "Truly I say to you — this poor widow put in more than all the contributors to the treasury.
41_12_44: For they all put in out of their surplus. But she, out of her poverty, put in all she owned — all she had to live on."
41_13_1: And as He was going out of the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, "Teacher, behold what wonderful stones and what wonderful buildings!"
41_13_2: And Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone shall be left upon another, which will not be torn down."
41_13_3: And as He was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were questioning Him privately,
41_13_4: "Tell us — when will these things be? And what will be the sign when all these things are going to be fulfilled?"
41_13_5: And Jesus began to say to them, "Take heed that no one misleads you.
41_13_6: Many will come in My name, saying, 'I am He!' — and will mislead many.
41_13_7: And when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be frightened. Those things must take place — but that is not yet the end.
41_13_8: For nation will arise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places. There will be famines. These things are merely the beginning of birth pangs.
41_13_9: But be on your guard. For they will deliver you to the courts. And you will be flogged in the synagogues — and you will stand before governors and kings for My sake, as a testimony to them.
41_13_10: And the gospel must first be preached to all the nations.
41_13_11: And when they arrest you and deliver you up, do not be anxious beforehand about what you are to say. But say whatever is given you in that hour. For it is not you who speak, but it is the Holy Spirit.
41_13_12: And brother will deliver brother to death, and a father his child. And children will rise up against parents, and have them put to death.
41_13_13: And you will be hated by all on account of My name — but the one who endures to the end, he shall be saved.
41_13_14: But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be — let the reader understand — then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
41_13_15: And let him who is on the housetop not go down, or enter in, to get anything out of his house.
41_13_16: And let him who is in the field not turn back to get his cloak.
41_13_17: But woe to those who are with child, and to those who are nursing babies in those days!
41_13_18: But pray that it may not happen in the winter.
41_13_19: For those days will be a time of tribulation such as has not occurred since the beginning of the creation which God created, until now — and never shall.
41_13_20: And unless the Lord had shortened those days, no life would have been saved. But for the sake of the elect whom He chose, He shortened the days.
41_13_21: And then if anyone says to you, 'Behold, here is the Christ!' — or, 'Behold, He is there!' — do not believe him.
41_13_22: For false Christs and false prophets will arise, and will show signs and wonders, in order, if possible, to lead the elect astray.
41_13_23: But take heed. Behold, I have told you everything in advance.
41_13_24: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
41_13_25: And the stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
41_13_26: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
41_13_27: And then He will send forth the angels, and will gather together His elect from the four winds — from the farthest end of the earth, to the farthest end of heaven.
41_13_28: Now learn the parable from the fig tree — when its branch has already become tender, and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near.
41_13_29: Even so, you too, when you see these things happening, recognize that He is near — right at the door.
41_13_30: Truly I say to you — this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
41_13_31: Heaven and earth will pass away — but My words will not pass away.
41_13_32: But of that day or hour no one knows — not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son — but the Father alone.
41_13_33: Take heed. Keep on the alert. For you do not know when the appointed time is.
41_13_34: It is like a man, away on a journey, who upon leaving his house and putting his slaves in charge — assigning to each one his task — also commanded the doorkeeper to stay on the alert.
41_13_35: Therefore, be on the alert. For you do not know when the master of the house is coming — whether in the evening, or at midnight, or when the rooster crows, or in the morning.
41_13_36: Lest he come suddenly and find you asleep.
41_13_37: And what I say to you, I say to all — be on the alert!"
41_14_1: Now the Passover and Unleavened Bread were two days off. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how to seize Him by stealth and kill Him.
41_14_2: For they were saying, "Not during the festival — lest there be a riot of the people."
41_14_3: And while He was in Bethany at the home of Simon the leper, reclining at table, there came a woman with an alabaster vial of very costly perfume of pure nard. She broke the vial and poured it over His head.
41_14_4: But some were indignantly remarking to one another, "Why has this perfume been wasted?
41_14_5: For this perfume might have been sold for over three hundred denarii, and the money given to the poor." And they were scolding her.
41_14_6: But Jesus said, "Let her alone. Why do you bother her? She has done a good deed to Me.
41_14_7: For the poor you always have with you, and whenever you wish, you can do them good. But you do not always have Me.
41_14_8: She has done what she could. She has anointed My body beforehand for the burial.
41_14_9: And truly I say to you — wherever the gospel is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done shall also be spoken of in memory of her."
41_14_10: And Judas Iscariot, who was one of the twelve, went off to the chief priests, in order to betray Him to them.
41_14_11: And when they heard it, they were glad and promised to give him money. And he began seeking how to betray Him at an opportune time.
41_14_12: And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was being sacrificed, His disciples said to Him, "Where do You want us to go and prepare for You to eat the Passover?"
41_14_13: And He sent two of His disciples, and said to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him.
41_14_14: And wherever he enters, say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Where is My guest room, in which I may eat the Passover with My disciples?"'
41_14_15: And he himself will show you a large upper room furnished and ready. And prepare for us there."
41_14_16: And the disciples went out, and came to the city, and found it just as He had told them. And they prepared the Passover.
41_14_17: And when it was evening, He came with the twelve.
41_14_18: And as they were reclining at table and eating, Jesus said, "Truly I say to you — one of you will betray Me. One who is eating with Me."
41_14_19: They began to be grieved and to say to Him one by one, "Surely not I?"
41_14_20: And He said to them, "It is one of the twelve — one who dips with Me in the bowl.
41_14_21: For the Son of Man is to go just as it is written of Him. But woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born."
41_14_22: And while they were eating, He took some bread, and after a blessing He broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take it — this is My body."
41_14_23: And when He had taken a cup and given thanks, He gave it to them. And they all drank from it.
41_14_24: And He said to them, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
41_14_25: Truly I say to you — I shall never again drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
41_14_26: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
41_14_27: And Jesus said to them, "You will all fall away. For it is written, 'I will strike down the shepherd — and the sheep shall be scattered.'
41_14_28: But after I have been raised, I will go before you to Galilee."
41_14_29: But Peter said to Him, "Even though all may fall away, yet I will not."
41_14_30: And Jesus said to him, "Truly I say to you — that you yourself this very night, before a rooster crows twice, shall three times deny Me."
41_14_31: But Peter kept saying insistently, "Even if I have to die with You, I will not deny You!" And they all were saying the same thing too.
41_14_32: And they came to a place named Gethsemane. And He said to His disciples, "Sit here until I have prayed."
41_14_33: And He took with Him Peter and James and John, and began to be very distressed and troubled.
41_14_34: And He said to them, "My soul is deeply grieved — to the point of death. Remain here, and keep watch."
41_14_35: And He went a little beyond them, and fell to the ground, and began to pray that, if it were possible, the hour might pass Him by.
41_14_36: And He was saying, "Abba — Father! All things are possible for You. Remove this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will."
41_14_37: And He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, "Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for one hour?
41_14_38: Keep watching and praying, that you may not come into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."
41_14_39: And again He went away and prayed, saying the same words.
41_14_40: And again He came and found them sleeping — for their eyes were very heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.
41_14_41: And He came the third time, and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough. The hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.
41_14_42: Arise — let us be going. Behold, the one who betrays Me is at hand!"
41_14_43: And immediately, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, came up, accompanied by a multitude with swords and clubs — from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
41_14_44: Now he who was betraying Him had given them a signal, saying, "Whomever I kiss, He is the one. Seize Him, and lead Him away under guard."
41_14_45: And after coming, he immediately went to Him, saying, "Rabbi!" — and kissed Him.
41_14_46: And they laid hands on Him and seized Him.
41_14_47: But a certain one of those who stood by drew his sword, and struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his ear.
41_14_48: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me, as you would against a robber?
41_14_49: Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me. But this has taken place that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
41_14_50: And they all left Him and fled.
41_14_51: And a certain young man was following Him, wearing nothing but a linen sheet over his naked body. And they seized him.
41_14_52: But he left the linen sheet behind, and escaped naked.
41_14_53: And they led Jesus away to the high priest. And all the chief priests, and the elders, and the scribes gathered together.
41_14_54: And Peter had followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the fire.
41_14_55: Now the chief priests and the whole Council kept trying to obtain testimony against Jesus to put Him to death — and they were not finding any.
41_14_56: For many were giving false testimony against Him — and yet their testimony was not consistent.
41_14_57: And some stood up and began to give false testimony against Him, saying,
41_14_58: "We heard Him say, 'I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.'"
41_14_59: And not even in this respect was their testimony consistent.
41_14_60: And the high priest stood up and came forward, and questioned Jesus, saying, "Do You make no answer? What is it that these men are testifying against You?"
41_14_61: But He kept silent, and made no answer. Again the high priest was questioning Him, and saying to Him, "Are You the Christ — the Son of the Blessed One?"
41_14_62: And Jesus said, "I am! And you shall see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven."
41_14_63: And tearing his clothes, the high priest said, "What further need do we have of witnesses?
41_14_64: You have heard the blasphemy. How does it seem to you?" And they all condemned Him to be deserving of death.
41_14_65: And some began to spit at Him, and to blindfold Him, and to beat Him with their fists, and to say to Him, "Prophesy!" And the officers received Him with slaps in the face.
41_14_66: And as Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant-girls of the high priest came.
41_14_67: And seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, "You, too, were with Jesus the Nazarene."
41_14_68: But he denied it, saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are talking about." And he went out onto the porch. And a rooster crowed.
41_14_69: And the maid saw him, and began once more to say to the bystanders, "This is one of them!"
41_14_70: But again he was denying it. And after a little while the bystanders were again saying to Peter, "Surely you are one of them, for you are a Galilean too."
41_14_71: But he began to curse and swear, "I do not know this man you are talking about!"
41_14_72: And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered how Jesus had made the remark to him, "Before a rooster crows twice, you will three times deny Me." And he began to weep.
41_15_1: And early in the morning the chief priests with the elders and scribes — and the whole Council — immediately held a consultation. And they bound Jesus and led Him away, and delivered Him up to Pilate.
41_15_2: And Pilate questioned Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" And answering him, He said, "You yourself say so."
41_15_3: And the chief priests began to accuse Him harshly.
41_15_4: And Pilate was questioning Him again, saying, "Do You make no answer? See how many charges they bring against You!"
41_15_5: But Jesus made no further answer — so that Pilate was amazed.
41_15_6: Now at the feast he used to release for them any one prisoner whom they requested.
41_15_7: And the man named Barabbas had been imprisoned with the insurrectionists — who had committed murder in the insurrection.
41_15_8: And the multitude went up and began asking him to do as he had been accustomed to do for them.
41_15_9: And Pilate answered them, saying, "Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?"
41_15_10: For he was aware that the chief priests had delivered Him up because of envy.
41_15_11: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude to ask him to release Barabbas for them instead.
41_15_12: And answering again, Pilate was saying to them, "Then what shall I do with Him whom you call the King of the Jews?"
41_15_14: But Pilate was saying to them, "Why, what evil has He done?" But they shouted all the more, "Crucify Him!"
41_15_15: And wishing to satisfy the multitude, Pilate released Barabbas for them — and after having Jesus scourged, he delivered Him to be crucified.
41_15_16: And the soldiers took Him away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) — and they called together the whole Roman cohort.
41_15_17: And they dressed Him up in purple, and after twisting a crown of thorns, they put it on Him.
41_15_18: And they began to acclaim Him, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
41_15_19: And they kept beating His head with a reed, and spitting on Him — and kneeling and bowing before Him.
41_15_20: And after they had mocked Him, they took the purple off Him, and put His own garments on Him. And they led Him out to crucify Him.
41_15_21: And they pressed into service a passer-by coming from the country — Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus — to bear His cross.
41_15_22: And they brought Him to the place Golgotha — which is translated, Place of a Skull.
41_15_23: And they tried to give Him wine mixed with myrrh — but He did not take it.
41_15_24: And they crucified Him, and divided up His garments among themselves, casting lots for them, to decide what each man should take.
41_15_25: And it was the third hour when they crucified Him.
41_15_26: And the inscription of the charge against Him read, "The King of the Jews."
41_15_27: And they crucified two robbers with Him — one on His right, and one on His left.
41_15_28: (And the Scripture was fulfilled which says, "And He was numbered with transgressors.")
41_15_29: And those passing by were hurling abuse at Him, wagging their heads, and saying, "Ha! You who destroy the temple, and rebuild it in three days,
41_15_30: save Yourself, and come down from the cross!"
41_15_31: In the same way the chief priests also, along with the scribes, were mocking Him among themselves and saying, "He saved others. He cannot save Himself!
41_15_32: Let this Christ — the King of Israel — come down from the cross right now, that we may see and believe." And those who were crucified with Him were also insulting Him.
41_15_33: And when the sixth hour had come, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour.
41_15_34: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" — which is translated, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"
41_15_35: And when some of the bystanders heard it, they began saying, "Behold, He is calling for Elijah!"
41_15_36: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave Him a drink, saying, "Let us see if Elijah will come to take Him down."
41_15_37: And Jesus uttered a loud cry, and breathed His last.
41_15_38: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
41_15_39: And when the centurion, who was standing right in front of Him, saw the way He breathed His last, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
41_15_40: And there were also some women looking on from a distance — among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the Less and Joses, and Salome.
41_15_41: And when He was in Galilee, they used to follow Him and minister to Him. And there were many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.
41_15_42: And when evening had already come, because it was the preparation day — that is, the day before the Sabbath —
41_15_43: Joseph of Arimathea came, a prominent member of the Council, who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God. And he gathered up courage and went in before Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.
41_15_44: And Pilate marveled that He was already dead. And summoning the centurion, he questioned him as to whether He was already dead.
41_15_45: And finding it out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
41_15_46: And Joseph bought a linen cloth. And taking Him down, he wrapped Him in the linen cloth, and laid Him in a tomb which had been hewn out in the rock — and he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
41_15_47: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were looking on to see where He was laid.
41_16_1: And when the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, that they might come and anoint Him.
41_16_2: And very early on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
41_16_3: And they were saying to one another, "Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?"
41_16_4: And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away. For it was extremely large.
41_16_5: And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting at the right, wearing a white robe — and they were amazed.
41_16_6: And he said to them, "Do not be amazed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who has been crucified. He has risen! He is not here. Behold, here is the place where they laid Him.
41_16_7: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, 'He is going before you into Galilee. There you will see Him — just as He said to you.'"
41_16_8: And they went out and fled from the tomb — for trembling and astonishment had gripped them. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
41_16_9: Now after He had risen early on the first day of the week, He first appeared to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had cast out seven demons.
41_16_10: She went and reported to those who had been with Him, while they were mourning and weeping.
41_16_11: And when they heard that He was alive, and had been seen by her, they refused to believe it.
41_16_12: And after that, He appeared in a different form to two of them, while they were walking along on their way to the country.
41_16_13: And they went away and reported it to the others. They did not believe them either.
41_16_14: And afterward He appeared to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at the table — and He reproached them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen Him after He had risen.
41_16_15: And He said to them, "Go into all the world and preach the gospel to all creation.
41_16_16: He who has believed and has been baptized shall be saved. But he who has disbelieved shall be condemned.
41_16_17: And these signs will accompany those who have believed: in My name they will cast out demons. They will speak with new tongues.
41_16_18: They will pick up serpents — and if they drink any deadly poison, it shall not hurt them. They will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover."
41_16_19: So then, when the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was received up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God.
41_16_20: And they went out and preached everywhere — while the Lord worked with them, and confirmed the word by the signs that followed.
40_1_1: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the Son of Abraham.
40_1_2: Abraham was the father of Isaac. And Isaac was the father of Jacob. And Jacob was the father of Judah and his brothers.
40_1_3: And Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. And Perez was the father of Hezron. And Hezron was the father of Ram.
40_1_4: And Ram was the father of Amminadab. And Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. And Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
40_1_5: And Salmon was the father of Boaz by Rahab. And Boaz was the father of Obed by Ruth. And Obed was the father of Jesse.
40_1_6: And Jesse was the father of David the king. And David was the father of Solomon by her who had been the wife of Uriah.
40_1_7: And Solomon was the father of Rehoboam. And Rehoboam was the father of Abijah. And Abijah was the father of Asa.
40_1_8: And Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat. And Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram. And Joram was the father of Uzziah.
40_1_9: And Uzziah was the father of Jotham. And Jotham was the father of Ahaz. And Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
40_1_10: And Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh. And Manasseh was the father of Amon. And Amon was the father of Josiah.
40_1_11: And Josiah was the father of Jeconiah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
40_1_12: And after the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel. And Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
40_1_13: And Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud. And Abiud was the father of Eliakim. And Eliakim was the father of Azor.
40_1_14: And Azor was the father of Zadok. And Zadok was the father of Achim. And Achim was the father of Eliud.
40_1_15: And Eliud was the father of Eleazar. And Eleazar was the father of Matthan. And Matthan was the father of Jacob.
40_1_16: And Jacob was the father of Joseph the husband of Mary — of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
40_1_17: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations — and from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations — and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
40_1_18: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was as follows. When His mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit.
40_1_19: And Joseph her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to disgrace her, planned to send her away secretly.
40_1_20: But while he was thinking about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife — for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
40_1_21: And she will bear a Son — and you shall call His name Jesus, for it is He who will save His people from their sins."
40_1_22: Now all this took place that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
40_1_23: "Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall bear a Son — and they shall call His name Immanuel," which translated means, "God with us."
40_1_24: And Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him — and took her as his wife,
40_1_25: and kept her a virgin until she gave birth to a Son. And he called His name Jesus.
40_2_1: Now after Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of Herod the king, behold, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,
40_2_2: saying, "Where is He who has been born King of the Jews? For we saw His star in the east, and have come to worship Him."
40_2_3: And when Herod the king heard it, he was troubled — and all Jerusalem with him.
40_2_4: And gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he began to inquire of them where the Christ was to be born.
40_2_5: And they said to him, "In Bethlehem of Judea — for so it has been written by the prophet:
40_2_6: 'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the leaders of Judah — for out of you shall come forth a Ruler, who will shepherd My people Israel.'"
40_2_7: Then Herod secretly called the magi, and ascertained from them the time the star appeared.
40_2_8: And he sent them to Bethlehem, and said, "Go and make careful search for the Child. And when you have found Him, report to me, that I too may come and worship Him."
40_2_9: And having heard the king, they went their way — and behold, the star which they had seen in the east went on before them, until it came and stood over where the Child was.
40_2_10: And when they saw the star, they rejoiced exceedingly with great joy.
40_2_11: And they came into the house and saw the Child with Mary His mother. And they fell down and worshiped Him. And opening their treasures, they presented to Him gifts of gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
40_2_12: And having been warned by God in a dream not to return to Herod, they departed for their own country by another way.
40_2_13: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Arise and take the Child and His mother, and flee to Egypt — and remain there until I tell you. For Herod is going to search for the Child to destroy Him."
40_2_14: And he arose and took the Child and His mother by night, and departed for Egypt.
40_2_15: And he was there until the death of Herod — that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "Out of Egypt I called My Son."
40_2_16: Then when Herod saw that he had been tricked by the magi, he became very enraged. And he sent and slew all the boys who were in Bethlehem and in all its environs, from two years old and under — according to the time which he had ascertained from the magi.
40_2_17: Then that which was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
40_2_18: "A voice was heard in Ramah — weeping and great mourning. Rachel weeping for her children. And she refused to be comforted, because they were no more."
40_2_19: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,
40_2_20: "Arise and take the Child and His mother, and go into the land of Israel. For those who sought the Child's life are dead."
40_2_21: And he arose and took the Child and His mother, and came into the land of Israel.
40_2_22: But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. And being warned by God in a dream, he departed for the regions of Galilee,
40_2_23: and came and resided in a city called Nazareth — that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled, "He shall be called a Nazarene."
40_3_1: Now in those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea, saying,
40_3_2: "Repent — for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."
40_3_3: For this is the one referred to by Isaiah the prophet, saying, "The voice of one crying in the wilderness — 'Prepare the way of the Lord. Make His paths straight!'"
40_3_4: Now John himself had a garment of camel's hair, and a leather belt about his waist — and his food was locusts and wild honey.
40_3_5: Then Jerusalem was going out to him, and all Judea, and all the district around the Jordan.
40_3_6: And they were being baptized by him in the Jordan river, as they confessed their sins.
40_3_7: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said to them, "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
40_3_8: Therefore bring forth fruit in keeping with your repentance.
40_3_9: And do not suppose that you can say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham for our father.' For I say to you that God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
40_3_10: And the axe is already laid at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
40_3_11: As for me, I baptize you with water for repentance — but He who is coming after me is mightier than I, and I am not fit to remove His sandals. He Himself will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
40_3_12: And His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He will thoroughly clear His threshing floor — and He will gather His wheat into the barn, but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire."
40_3_13: Then Jesus arrived from Galilee at the Jordan, coming to John to be baptized by him.
40_3_14: But John tried to prevent Him, saying, "I have need to be baptized by You — and do You come to me?"
40_3_15: But Jesus answering said to him, "Permit it at this time — for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he permitted Him.
40_3_16: And after being baptized, Jesus went up immediately from the water — and behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming upon Him.
40_3_17: And behold, a voice out of the heavens, saying, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well-pleased."
40_4_1: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
40_4_2: And after He had fasted forty days and forty nights, He then became hungry.
40_4_3: And the tempter came and said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread."
40_4_4: But He answered and said, "It is written, 'Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.'"
40_4_5: Then the devil took Him into the holy city, and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.
40_4_6: And he said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down — for it is written, 'He will give His angels charge concerning You. And on their hands they will bear You up, lest You strike Your foot against a stone.'"
40_4_7: Jesus said to him, "On the other hand, it is written, 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
40_4_8: Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
40_4_9: And he said to Him, "All these things will I give You, if You fall down and worship me."
40_4_10: Then Jesus said to him, "Be gone, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only.'"
40_4_11: Then the devil left Him — and behold, angels came and began to minister to Him.
40_4_12: Now when He heard that John had been taken into custody, He withdrew into Galilee.
40_4_13: And leaving Nazareth, He came and settled in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali.
